dashboard.title: Help — Dashboard

actions.label: Quick actions
actions.text:
At the top you find shortcuts to common actions, so you do not have to dig through the menus every time.

Depending on your rights and active modules you may see, among others:
• New day task via favourites
• Plan a new day task
• Add location
• Add worker or View workers
• Who works where today
• Manual clock-in
• Which tasks today
• View roster

Not every button is always visible. That depends on your role and on active modules, such as Time or the calendar.

actions.label: What’s new?
actions.text:
If the What’s new? card appears at the top, something recently changed in WinProx.

The card stays visible for up to one week. Click it to view the recent changes under Help → New. After that the card disappears.

If a newer note appears later, the card shows again.

actions.label: Overview
actions.text:
Under the Dashboard title you find cards with current counts and attention points.

Examples are:
• Open reports.
• Open tasks.
• Who is present now, if Time is active.

Some cards appear only when there is something to do — for example reports to review, attention points in Time, a new worker to check, or open requests or IoT alarms.

Click a card to go straight to the matching screen.

Open leave, time-off-in-lieu, sick or Other requests appear as a separate card. You see the count per type. Click it to go to Time → Requests.

If photos with an absence are older than 5 months, a card appears. They will be deleted within a month. Click it to view them under Requests and keep your own copy.

actions.label: WinProx on your desktop
actions.text:
You do not need to install WinProx from an app store. You can still open management as a separate application.

• Chrome or Edge: click Add to desktop at the bottom of the sidebar. WinProx then opens in its own window, without an address bar, and a shortcut is placed on your desktop.
• Firefox: this feature is not available.
• Mac with Safari: choose Add to Dock in the File menu.
• iPhone or iPad: use Share to add WinProx as an icon on your home screen.

Important: management is meant for a computer or tablet. The punch clock on your phone uses a separate shortcut.

actions.label: Starter template
actions.text:
New organisations see the question Would you like a hand getting started? on the dashboard.

You can choose what you want to use WinProx for:
• Own locations.
• Customer locations.
• Vehicles and fleet.

Based on your choice, WinProx creates a small sample environment with teams, categories, one location and units.

If you choose working at customers, you can also indicate your organisation size:
• 1–5
• 6–20
• 21+

You can also choose to start yourself.

Good to know: the starter template is not a fixed sector system. It is only meant to get you started faster. Afterwards you can add or rename locations, teams and units yourself.

actions.label: Print briefing
actions.text:
With Print briefing you open a printable overview of today’s open tasks, grouped by team.

Handy to print and hand to workers on the floor.

actions.label: Trial period
actions.text:
During the trial period you can use WinProx with:
• Up to 5 licences.
• Up to 50 units.
• Up to 10 documents.
• Time, including punch clock.

On the dashboard you see how many days your trial still lasts.

More about plans and limits is under Organisation → Subscription.

actions.label: Add a report
actions.text:
With Add report you quickly create a new report. That happens in two steps:

1. Choose the location or unit and enter a description.
2. Then create a task for the team that should handle the report.

That way you can link the needed action to a report at once.

The full list of reports is under Work → Reports.

actions.label: Recent reports
actions.text:
At the bottom of the dashboard you find the most recent reports.

Per report you see, among other things:
• The description.
• The location or unit.
• The time.
• The status.
• Who created the report.

Did the reporter complete confirmation via the QR code? Then the Reporter confirmed mark appears.

A newly created report can be temporarily highlighted in the list.

dashboard.status_note: The status on the dashboard is determined by the tasks linked to the report.

statuses.new: There is at least one task that has not started yet.
statuses.in_progress: At least one task is in progress.
statuses.done: All tasks are completed. An admin can then close the report.
statuses.closed: All tasks are closed. The report is fully finished.

issues.list.title: Help — Issues

actions.label: Add issue
actions.text: Create an issue via the popup in the desktop version of Winprox or after scanning a QR code at a unit via the QR portal. A task is always automatically created which you can refine later on the Tasks page.

actions.label: Plan inspection round
actions.text: Separate button next to Add issue: pick at least 2 stops (units), interval and team in one form. Creates a recurring issue with round stops and starts the first task immediately. The rounds list is under Work → Inspection rounds. With Time + GPS work visits, today's stops appear on Clock Point → Where do I need to go today after clock-in.

actions.label: Interval
actions.text: How often the issue recurs (e.g. every 2 weeks, every month, every quarter, every year).

actions.label: Lead (days)
actions.text: How many days before the due date the task is created (e.g. 7 days for monthly tasks).

actions.label: First due date
actions.text: The date the first round is due. The task is created earlier according to the lead.

actions.label: Stops
actions.text: Pick at least 2 units (any locations). Tick and drag in the same list per location (1 = first stop). Only units with unit checks appear in the list.

actions.label: Task note
actions.text: Optional instruction for the team on this task. Leave empty to use the issue description.

actions.label: Print briefing
actions.text: Print an overview of open tasks per team.

actions.label: Filters
actions.text: Combine status, team, search term, recurring and inspection rounds to refine the list. The search term looks in the description (source text and completed translations), location, address, postcode, city, unit and reporter. Press GO! to apply. Inspection rounds have their own screen under Work → Inspection rounds.

actions.label: Download report
actions.text: Export the filtered results (not only the current page; max. 5000 rows): CSV (table for Excel) or Print (same card layout as the backoffice list; Ctrl+P to PDF). Uses the same filters as the list.

actions.label: Approve
actions.text: Issues created via the QR portal wait for approval. Approve so content becomes visible on public pages.

actions.label: Reporter confirmed
actions.text: QR reports where the reporter confirmed the email link show the Reporter confirmed pill on the list, the dashboard and the issue detail.

issues.list.status_note: Issue status is derived automatically from the tasks on that issue.

statuses.new: New issue; at least one task has not been started yet.
statuses.in_progress: Follow-up is underway — a task has been started or is in progress.
statuses.done: All tasks have been completed by the team.
statuses.closed: An administrator has confirmed and closed everything.

issues.inspection_rounds.title: Help — Inspection rounds

actions.label: What is this screen?
actions.text: This screen lists inspection rounds only: rounds with at least two unit stops, recurring or one-time. Create regular issues via Work → Issues, not here.

actions.label: Plan inspection round
actions.text: Enter description, team and stops. Search/choose on the left, drag the route on the right. Recurring on for interval/lead, or off for a one-time round. Starts the first task immediately.

actions.label: Favorite
actions.text: Star a round to mark it as a favorite. Favorites sort to the top and can be filtered. Closed favorites stay findable via “Favorites only”.

actions.label: Copy
actions.text: Opens the plan popup with stops and title prefilled. Defaults to a one-time round due today; choose team/worker and confirm.

actions.label: Interval
actions.text: How often the round recurs (e.g. every 2 weeks, every month, every quarter, every year).

actions.label: Lead (days)
actions.text: How many days before the due date the task is created (e.g. 7 days for monthly rounds).

actions.label: First due date
actions.text: The date the first round is due. The task is created earlier according to the lead.

actions.label: Stops
actions.text: Search and tick on the left; drag the route on the right (1 = first stop). Whole-location sites = one grey row. Only units with unit checks. At least 2 stops.

actions.label: Task note
actions.text: Optional instruction for the team on this task. Leave empty to use the round description.

actions.label: Print briefing
actions.text: Print an overview of open tasks per team.

actions.label: Filters
actions.text: Narrow by status, team or search term. Search looks in description, location, address, postcode, city, unit and reporter. Press GO! to apply. This screen always shows inspection rounds only.

actions.label: Download report
actions.text: Export the filtered results (not only the current page; max. 5000 rows): CSV (table for Excel) or Print (same card layout as the backoffice list; Ctrl+P to PDF).

issues.inspection_rounds.status_note: Round status is derived automatically from the tasks on that round.

statuses.new: New round; at least one task has not been started yet.
statuses.in_progress: Follow-up is underway — a task has been started or is in progress.
statuses.done: All tasks on the round have been completed by the team.
statuses.closed: An administrator has confirmed and closed the round.

issues.show.title: Help — Issue detail

actions.label: Add task
actions.text: Add a task to an existing issue or edit an existing task. Give a clear, concrete description of the problem or action to be performed (e.g., "Printer prints dirty"). Select a specific due date via the calendar. Leave this blank if the task should be picked up directly or flexibly. Determine the urgency of the task (Prio 1 to 3). This field is exclusive to administrators to prevent priority inflation on the shop floor. Assign the task to the right operational team. This team receives a direct notification. Workers start tasks via the unit QR portal after signing in via the Clock Point QR.

actions.label: Post update
actions.text: Add a note or photo to the issue; this will be shown on the portal.

actions.label: Approve
actions.text: Approve QR issues before description and photos become publicly visible.

actions.label: Description translation
actions.text: On approved issues, pick a language (NL, EN, FR, DE, ES, IT) next to the description. The text is translated automatically after approval by WinProx (periodically). If a translation is not ready yet, you will see «Not translated yet». Lists and search show the source text until then. Active announcements and documents follow the same pattern on the location page. Tasks with their own description show the translated text in lists and the portal once ready.

actions.label: Task translations
actions.text: In the task edit form you can manually update the task description per language (NL, EN, FR, DE, ES, IT). Useful when the automatic translation by WinProx (periodically) is wrong or still missing. Only available when the task has its own description. Saving finalises the translation for that language.

actions.label: Reporter confirmed
actions.text: QR reports where the reporter confirmed the email link show the Reporter confirmed pill on the list, the dashboard and the issue detail.

issues.show.status_note: Change issue status by updating the tasks.

statuses.new: Waiting for at least one task to start.
statuses.in_progress: At least one task is actively being worked on.
statuses.done: All tasks are completed; close the issue when everything is confirmed.

actions.label: Interval
actions.text: How often the issue recurs (e.g. every 2 weeks, every month, every quarter, every year).

actions.label: Lead (days)
actions.text: How many days before the due date the task is created (e.g. 7 days for monthly tasks).

actions.label: First due date
actions.text: The date the first round is due. The task is created earlier according to the lead.

actions.label: Inspection round stops
actions.text: Search and tick on the left; drag the route on the right (1 = first stop). Whole-location sites appear as one grey row. Only units with unit checks. At least 2 stops.

actions.label: Select all units
actions.text: Adds all available stops to the route. You can then untick individual stops in the route.

actions.label: Task note
actions.text: Optional instruction for the team on this task. Leave empty to use the issue description.

tasks.list.title: Help — Tasks

actions.label: Filter by team
actions.text: Show only tasks for one operational team. Team managers see only their teams by default.

actions.label: Open task
actions.text: Click a task for detail, status changes and the link to the issue.

actions.label: Recurring
actions.text: Filter recurring tasks (Recurring pill). These come from recurring issues with a planned due date per cycle.

actions.label: Download report
actions.text: Export the filtered results (not only the current page; max. 5000 rows): CSV (table for Excel) or Print (same card layout as the backoffice list; Ctrl+P to PDF). Uses the same filters as the list.

tasks.list.status_note: Statuses are often updated automatically via the unit QR portal. You can also adjust them manually.

statuses.new: Task has been created and is waiting for the team to start.
statuses.in_progress: The team is working on it.
statuses.done: Work is finished by the worker; an administrator can close it.
statuses.closed: Task has been confirmed and closed.

tasks.show.title: Help — Task detail

actions.label: Recurring
actions.text: If the task comes from a recurring issue, you see the Recurring pill and this cycle's planned due date. A new cycle task is only created after the previous one is done or closed — so open tasks do not pile up.

actions.label: Inspection round
actions.text: For an inspection round you see progress per stop (OK, Not OK, skipped, open). Date/time and worker are compact. Below that: checklist points that were not OK — the evidence for the customer. On each stop’s unit QR portal the worker sees the same progress; the task completes automatically when all stops are done. You can also complete or close an open round here (with a reason).

actions.label: Print
actions.text: Inspection rounds only. Opens a printable page of this cycle: stops, Not OK checklist points, note and photos. Ctrl+P to PDF for the customer.

actions.label: Assign team
actions.text: Choose an operational team and save. You can also change an existing assignment.

actions.label: Change status
actions.text: Set the task to In progress, Completed or Closed depending on progress.

actions.label: Description translation
actions.text: If the task has its own description (not only the issue text), it is translated automatically by WinProx (periodically). In the task edit form you can manually update that description per language (NL, EN, FR, DE, ES, IT). Useful when the automatic translation is wrong or still missing. Saving finalises the translation for that language. Without its own description, the task follows the linked issue translation.

actions.label: Open issue
actions.text: Go to the linked issue for context, photos and additional tasks.

actions.label: Reading and follow-up
actions.text: Shown only on ESG measurement tasks. Lists the recorded value, any threshold alarm, the measurement task, and a follow-up task. Open on Reading goes to the filtered measurements overview; on Measurement task opens the linked task.

tasks.show.status_note: On the shop floor, workers start and complete tasks via the unit QR portal (after signing in via Clock Point QR), or via Clock Point with an open GPS work visit at that location.

statuses.done: Worker reports the work as done.

actions.label: What is a location?
actions.text:
A location is a physical place where you work. That can be a building, a company site, a customer address or a construction site.

You can later attach units to each location. Those are rooms, machines, toilets, vehicles or other assets, for example. A unit can have its own QR code so users can view information, submit reports or register data.

Tip: create the location first. Then, on that location’s detail page, manage units, QR codes, documents and announcements.

actions.label: Add a location
actions.text:
Click Add and enter the basic details:
• Location name.
• Location address.

Save to create the location. You can then attach units to it.

Tip: enter the address as completely as possible, including house number, postcode and city. That matters for maps, GPS features and any filings.

actions.label: Open a location
actions.text:
Click a location in the list to open its detail page.

There you can manage, among other things:
• Units and QR codes: rooms, machines, devices and other assets at this location.
• Documents: documents that belong with the location.
• Announcements: information you want to share with users.
• Extra settings: settings specific to this location.

actions.label: Import locations
actions.text:
Already have a list of locations in Excel or CSV? You can import several locations at once, so you do not have to create them one by one.

What data is required?
Each row must contain at least one of these:
• A location name.
• A full address with street, postcode and city.

You can also import extra data:
• House number.
• Country.
• Notes.
• GPS coordinates.
• The Declaration of works number (if CIAO is active).

Important: WinProx checks the whole import file before creating locations. If column headers are wrong or required data is missing in a row, the entire import is refused. That way you avoid loading only part of your locations.

Where do you find the Declaration of works number?
You find it on the Social Security portal, under Declaration of works. Open the declaration for that workplace.

No access yourself? Ask the person who submitted the declaration, for example your customer or main contractor.

For some cleaning declarations, WinProx can also read the number automatically from a CIAO QR code or link.

actions.label: Recent location imports
actions.text:
Here you find an overview of location imports from the last 30 days.

Per import you see:
• The imported file name.
• The import date.
• How many locations were created.

Undo import
Imported the wrong file by mistake? You can undo the import.

WinProx then removes the locations created in that import. That only works when those locations still have no units, reports, documents or announcements linked.

Once a location is in use, the import can no longer be fully undone. That way WinProx avoids deleting data that is already in use.

actions.label: GPS pin
actions.text:
For some features, such as GPS work visits in Time or CIAO, the location must sit exactly on the map.

A normal address is sometimes not precise enough. In that case you can set the correct GPS coordinates yourself.

How do you set the GPS pin?
1. Click the red Google Maps icon.
2. Search for the location address.
3. Move the red pin to the exact place on the map.
4. Copy the coordinates.
5. Paste them in WinProx.

Use this format:
51.336167, 3.236306

The first value is latitude, the second longitude.

You can use the same approach to set the GPS pin of an individual unit.

actions.label: Declaration of works (DDT)
actions.text:
This field is only visible when CIAO is active.

Enter the technical number of the NSSO Declaration of works for this workplace.

The number has 13 characters and is linked to that specific workplace.

Where do you find this number?
You can find it:
• On the Social Security portal.
• In e-Box Enterprise.
• On the declaration QR code or poster on site.

Important for CIAO: to process clock punches correctly, WinProx needs a valid DDT together with the workplace address or GPS location.

If a valid number or the required location information is missing, CIAO punches for that workplace are skipped.

Unsure about the number? Ask the person who manages the declaration.

actions.label: Show inactive locations
actions.text:
No longer using a location? You can Deactivate it.

The location then leaves the normal list, but is not deleted. That keeps the existing history.

Turn on Show inactive to make these locations visible again.

You can then:
• Activate them again if you want to use them.
• Open them to consult the existing data.

Tip: deactivating is usually better than deleting. That way you keep the history of locations you no longer use.

actions.label: Location translations
actions.text:
WinProx translates location names automatically into the available languages.

Is a translation wrong or missing? You can adjust the name yourself in the edit form.

You can set the name per language: Dutch, English, French, German, Spanish and Italian.

Select the language, enter the correct name and save. Your adjusted translation then becomes the fixed name for that language.

actions.label: What is a category for?
actions.text:
A category groups units of the same type. Think of washrooms, offices, fitness equipment or machines. That way you can organise your units and find them easily.

You can also link a team to a category. Reports and tasks can then reach the team responsible for that type of unit. A report about washrooms, for example, goes to the washroom team.

actions.label: The name in other languages
actions.text:
WinProx translates the category name automatically into the available languages.

Is a translation wrong or missing? You can correct it yourself in the category form. Select the language, enter the right name and save. Your corrected translation then becomes the fixed name for that language.

actions.label: What happens on the QR page?
actions.text:
The settings below decide which features are available when someone scans a unit’s QR code.

You set these options at category level. New units in the category take the settings over automatically.

Change something later? Units that still use the category’s standard settings follow along. If you chose your own settings for a particular unit, those stay as they are.

You set those exceptions on the unit itself, under Per-unit portal options.

Please note: Show previous reports is an exception. This setting always applies to every unit in the category and cannot be changed separately per unit.

actions.label: Allow GPS location
actions.text:
Useful for mobile units that often change place, such as a crane or a large machine.

Through the QR code, the user can say where the unit is at that moment. Administration then knows where the equipment is, and you can find it more easily.

You manage this setting only at category level. You cannot change it separately per unit.

actions.label: Reservable
actions.text:
Turn this on when users need to reserve a unit in advance for a period of time.

For example a meeting room, a company vehicle or a key.

The Reserve tile appears on the QR page when this feature is switched on for both the category and the unit.

Reporting a defect or a problem remains possible through the ordinary report.

actions.label: Allow unit checks
actions.text:
With a unit check, a worker can quickly confirm whether something is in order.

For example after a cleaning round or during a safety check. The worker simply marks everything OK or Not OK.

The Unit check tile appears only when this feature is switched on for both the category and the unit.

A unit check is a check, not a record of a reading such as a temperature or a mileage.

actions.label: Require contact details
actions.text:
Turn this on when you want visitors to enter their contact details before they can send a report via the QR code.

Anyone who is not signed in to WinProx must then enter their first name, last name and email address.

Workers who are already signed in do not have to do this.

This requirement works only when it is also switched on for that unit.

actions.label: Require email confirmation
actions.text:
Do you want to check that the email address given is correct? Turn this option on.

The reporter receives an email with a confirmation link. The report is created and processed only after they click that link.

Without confirmation, no report is created.

Workers who are already signed in to WinProx do not have to confirm their email address again.

This setting works only when it is also switched on for that unit.

actions.label: Allow unit measurements
actions.text:
With unit measurements, users can record a reading or a status via the QR code.

For example:
• The mileage of a vehicle.
• The temperature of a room.
• A particular reading or technical status.

You set up the measurement fields you want to use under Work → Unit measurements.

The measurements tile appears only when this feature is switched on for both the category and the unit.

Unit measurements are different from unit checks. With a unit check, someone says whether something is in order. With a unit measurement, a specific value is recorded.

actions.label: Show previous reports
actions.text:
This option is on by default.

When someone scans a unit’s QR code, they can see which reports for that unit are still open.

Do you not want visitors to see this information? Turn the option off.

That can be useful for hotel rooms, toilets or other spaces where you would rather not show open reports to visitors.

Important: this setting applies to every unit in the category. You cannot change it separately per unit.

actions.label: Add unit
actions.text: Add an object/machine/asset/space with QR token and default team. A unit can be diverse: a machine, room, vehicle, aerial work platform, fitness device, etc. Portal behaviour (reports, reservations, checks, …) follows the chosen category by default; see Advanced portal options for exceptions.

actions.label: Work-visit pin
actions.text: Under Advanced portal options. Same Google Maps icon: search, red pin, copy, paste. Empty = no Start work on this unit.

actions.label: Works declaration (DDT)
actions.text: Only visible when CIAO is on. Per location, enter the technical number (13 characters) of the NSSO works declaration for that site. Find it on the social security portal, in e-Box Enterprise, or on the site QR/poster. Without a valid DDT (and address or GPS), CIAO punches are skipped.

actions.label: Location translations
actions.text: In the location edit form you can manually update the name per language (NL, EN, FR, DE, ES, IT). Useful when the automatic translation by WinProx (periodically) is wrong or still missing. Saving finalises the translation for that language.

actions.label: Unit translations
actions.text: In the unit edit form you can manually update name and description per language (NL, EN, FR, DE, ES, IT). Useful when the automatic translation by WinProx (periodically) is wrong or still missing. Saving finalises the translation for that language.

actions.label: Advanced portal options
actions.text: In the unit edit form, portal checkboxes are grouped in the collapsible «Portal options per unit» menu (below Category), similar to Translation. Prefer setting these on the category: units inherit those values automatically. Open the submenu only when one unit must differ. Hover over Category or Portal options per unit for help in a tooltip.

actions.label: What is in the submenu?
actions.text: Public reports, reservations, unit checks (+ optional checklist), unit measurements (+ measure fields), required contact details and email confirmation. GPS location is category-only, not per unit. Both category and unit must be on before a feature appears on the QR portal.

actions.label: External ID
actions.text: Only visible with API access (Corporate, or trial with API). Map the unit to your external facility software (IWMS, CMMS, ERP, …). External systems can then push unit checks via POST /api/v1/units/checks.

actions.label: Checklist (unit check)
actions.text: Optionally link a checklist to the unit (templates under Work → Checklists, shared or from the category’s teams). On Unit check in the portal the worker ticks each item before OK is saved.

actions.label: Bulk units
actions.text: Create a range of units at once. Enter start number (as text so leading zeros are kept, e.g. 01 or 201), count, optional digits (padding; leave empty to auto-detect from the start number), prefix (e.g. Room + space) and suffix (e.g. -A). Examples: 01; Room 20–22; Room 201–203; Room 501. The preview lists names live; duplicates are highlighted in red and block Create. Optionally assign all new units to one category. Under Advanced portal options you can set the same flags as for a single unit for the whole range (reports, checks, measurements, contact). Roster code, photos and GPS pin stay per unit. Maximum 500 units per bulk.

actions.label: Import units
actions.text: Import units for this location via CSV or Excel (.xlsx). Required: unit_name. Optional: description, category_name, external_id (API mapping) and flags allow_reservations, allow_unit_checks, allow_unit_measurements, require_reporter_contact, require_reporter_email_verification, public_reports_enabled (1/0, yes/no — empty = defaults as manual create). Location columns are not needed. Wrong headers or missing required fields reject the entire import with a clear error per row. Categories are created automatically if they do not exist yet.

actions.label: Recent imports
actions.text: After an import, an overview of recent imports (30 days) for this location appears. Per import you see file name, date and unit count. Click Undo import to remove units without issues or tasks. Empty categories created only by the import are cleaned up. The location itself is kept.

actions.label: QR print sheet
actions.text: Download a Word file with QR stickers (Avery/HERMA) or full-page print sheets (A6/A5/A4, 1 QR per page) for all units at this location. You can also generate free dynamic QR codes that are not yet linked to a unit. These can first be attached to a unit and then assigned to a unit via the same QR code. Administrators/employees can link all units to these dynamic QR codes. Team workers can only link units that are connected to their team.

actions.label: GPS
actions.text: View a unit's location history via the pop-up once GPS coordinates are available. Click 'Open in Maps' to open the location directly in Google Maps.

actions.label: Documents & announcements
actions.text: Manage documents and announcements for the unit QR portal. Documents: turn on «Active» to publish in the portal. Without «Field workers only», any visitor can view and download the file. With «Field workers only», only a field worker signed in to the portal (name + icon) can see and download it — not via the admin screen with email login. Inactive documents remain visible only here. Active documents are translated automatically by WinProx (periodically; description); the edit form shows a translation preview per language. The title stays in the source language.

calendar.title: Help — Calendar

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: Time overview of scheduled tasks, created issues and unit reservations. Admin screens show everything clearly — no blur here.

actions.label: View
actions.text: Choose month, week or day. Weeks start on Monday. Today is highlighted in emerald; days outside the selected month are grey.

actions.label: Navigation
actions.text: Browse with previous, today and next. The URL remembers view, type, date, location and (for reservations) category — useful to share or bookmark.

actions.label: Type
actions.text: Switch between Tasks (default), Issues and Reservations. Each type shows different items and status pills.

actions.label: Tasks
actions.text: Shows tasks with a planned date or due date — including cycles from recurring issues. Only tasks from approved issues. Sorted by priority. Click opens the task detail (reference number + status pill).

actions.label: Issues
actions.text: Shows issues on their creation date (when they came in). Click opens the issue detail.

actions.label: Reservations
actions.text: Shows active pending holds and confirmed bookings (cancelled or expired do not appear here). Per item: unit and time slot; in week and day view also the guest name. Click opens the reservations list.

actions.label: Filters
actions.text: Location: all locations or one. For Reservations a second filter appears for reservable categories. Switching back to Tasks or Issues clears that category filter.

actions.label: Month grid
actions.text: Up to five items per day; then «+X more». Use week or day view for the full list of that day.

actions.label: Week and day
actions.text: List cards per day. In day view, browse pages with previous/next when there are more than 50 items.

actions.label: Briefing
actions.text: Print briefing opens a printable overview of tasks for that day, grouped by team. In Tasks mode the briefing date follows the selected calendar day.

calendar.status_note: For Tasks and Issues, pills follow the task or issue status below. For Reservations: pending (awaiting email confirmation) or confirmed — those block overlapping slots.

statuses.new: Planned or new, not yet started.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: Reservations are for shareable timed resources: meeting rooms, vehicles, keys, … Not for defect reports — those stay on Issue → task.

actions.label: Enable
actions.text: Turn on Reservable on the category. Units in that category inherit Allow reservations automatically. The unit QR then shows the Reserve tile (both category and unit must be on). To override per unit, use Advanced portal options when editing the unit.

actions.label: Guest flow
actions.text: A guest books via QR, gets a 30-minute hold and confirms by email. Change or cancel via the mail link or again via QR (name/email remembered in a cookie).

actions.label: Admin
actions.text: Here you create immediately confirmed reservations, change time slots and cancel bookings. Open the calendar for the time-block overview.

actions.label: Filters
actions.text: Filter by status and location, or search by guest, email, unit or location. Press GO! to apply. Upcoming reservations are shown by default.

actions.label: Download report
actions.text: Export the filtered reservations as CSV or print (Ctrl+P to PDF) in the same card layout as this list. Same filters as the screen; max. 5000 rows.

actions.label: Overlap
actions.text: The system blocks overlapping slots for confirmed and active pending holds. Expired pending holds lapse after 30 minutes.

actions.label: Colleague users
actions.text:
Here you manage the colleagues who work with WinProx on a computer. They sign in with their email address and password.

Please note: you do not manage workers on the floor here. They use WinProx via the QR code on the punch clock and do not need an email account for that.

For each colleague you see:
• Name.
• Email address.
• Role.
• Whether the account is active.

actions.label: Roles
actions.text:
WinProx has two roles.

Administrator

An administrator can manage the organisation. They can, among other things:
• Manage colleague users.
• Change company details.
• Manage the subscription.

You can have more than one administrator in one organisation.

Employee

An employee can work in WinProx, but cannot manage user accounts, company details or the subscription.

Choose this role for colleagues who follow the day-to-day work, but do not need to be an administrator.

actions.label: Add a colleague
actions.text:
Click Add user to create a new colleague.

Fill in:
• Name.
• Work email address.
• Language.
• Role: Administrator or Employee.

actions.label: Set a password
actions.text:
You have two options:

• You choose a password yourself and give it to the colleague.
• You let WinProx send an email. The colleague can then set a password via the link in that email.

Editing an existing colleague? Leave the password fields empty if the current password should stay as it is.

actions.label: Email for new reports
actions.text: You can also set the colleague to receive an email each time someone submits a new report via a unit QR code.

actions.label: Locations
actions.text:
For an employee you can choose which locations they can access.

Tick the locations you want.

• One or more locations selected: the employee can access those locations.
• No locations selected: the employee can access all locations.

An administrator always has access to all locations. This limit applies only to employees.

actions.label: Sign in with Microsoft
actions.text:
The sign-in screen can show Sign in with Microsoft.

Colleagues can use it to sign in with their Microsoft account, as long as that email address matches the email address of their WinProx account.

No new WinProx account is created. Microsoft is only used to sign in the existing colleague.

Workers do not use this sign-in method. They sign in via the QR code on the punch clock.

actions.label: Punch clock
actions.text:
Should a colleague also be able to clock in, besides the back-office work? Then you can link that person to a worker profile.

Open the colleague to edit them and choose a Punch clock team. This field is only visible when the punch clock is switched on.

What happens next?

WinProx automatically creates a worker profile with the same name.

The colleague can then also clock in on the punch clock, where they are recognised by their name and icon.

Important: the worker profile does not count as an extra person or licence. The colleague remains one person in your organisation.

actions.label: Active or inactive
actions.text:
Is a colleague leaving your organisation, or should they no longer be able to sign in? Then you can Deactivate the account.

A deactivated colleague can no longer sign in to WinProx. The account and its details are kept.

Do you want to allow access again later? Then you can Activate the account again.

You recognise your own account by the label You. To stop you from locking yourself out by accident, you cannot deactivate your own account here.

actions.label: Licences
actions.text:
Colleagues and workers share the licences of your WinProx subscription.

A colleague who also has a worker profile so they can clock in counts as only one licence.

You do not pay twice for someone who both works in the back office and clocks in on the punch clock.

actions.label: What is a team for?
actions.text:
A team groups workers who do the same kind of work. Think of a cleaning team, a technical service or reception.

Workers in the same team see the same tasks. One team is enough to get started. Create an extra team only when there really is a different group.

You can link a team to one or more categories. Reports and tasks for units in those categories then reach the team.

actions.label: Creating a team
actions.text:
You find Teams via People → Teams.

Give the team a name, for example Hotel or Facility. Then add the workers who belong to that team.

A team leader is not required.

As long as the team has no workers yet, you can delete the team.

actions.label: Team name in other languages
actions.text:
WinProx translates the team name automatically into the available languages: Dutch, English, French, German, Spanish and Italian.

Is a translation wrong or missing? You can correct it yourself:
1. Open the team form.
2. Choose the language.
3. Enter the name you want.
4. Save.

Your corrected translation then becomes the fixed name for that language.

actions.label: Workers
actions.text:
A worker does not sign in with an email address and password. On Clock Point that person chooses their name and a personal icon. That happens on one phone.

You can optionally add a PIN or a passkey.

On the team page you see for each worker whether the profile is active, blocked or a team leader. You change the details via Edit.

Do you have many workers? You can view and manage the full list via People → Workers.

actions.label: Signing in on Clock Point
actions.text:
Workers sign in with the Clock Point QR code.

Is Time on? Then they use the same QR code to clock in and out as well.

You will find the Clock Point QR code button on this page. If Time is on, you manage and print the QR codes via Time → Clock Points.

actions.label: How long does a worker stay signed in?
actions.text:
For each team you decide how long a worker stays signed in after scanning the Clock Point QR code.

You set this under Worker session duration:
• Daily: 14 hours. This is the default.
• Weekly: 6 working days.
• Custom hours: you enter the number of hours yourself.

actions.label: Releasing an icon, PIN or device
actions.text: Open Edit for the worker to manage the security settings.

actions.label: Reset icon
actions.text:
With Reset icon you clear the icon, the PIN, any passkey and the linked phone.

The worker can then sign in again. This is useful, for example, with a lost phone, a lockout or a wrongly chosen icon.

If a PIN is active, this button is not available. The list then also does not show No icon confirmed. The Time clock block stays hidden until there is something to do.

actions.label: Other security actions
actions.text:
The following buttons appear only when they apply:
• Allow new device: appears when a phone is linked.
• Reset PIN: appears when a PIN is set.
• Remove passkey: appears when a passkey is set.

A team leader can also release a teammate’s icon in the portal.

actions.label: Team leader
actions.text:
Via Edit you make someone a team leader, or you withdraw that role.

A team leader can, through the Clock Point portal:
• Release a teammate’s icon.
• Manage workers.
• Take photos.

actions.label: Sites
actions.text:
At the top of the team list you can choose a site. You then see, in each team, only the workers who may clock in at that site.

Workers without a fixed site, and teams that may clock in anywhere, stay visible.

With All locations you show everyone again. The count next to a team only includes the workers who are visible at that moment.

actions.label: Assign sites to a worker
actions.text:
Open the worker via Edit and choose one or more sites.

If you leave this field empty, that person may clock in anywhere. That is also the default for existing workers.

On Clock Point a worker sees their name only at the assigned sites, unless the team has May clock in anywhere (floater team) switched on.

actions.label: May clock in anywhere
actions.text:
Switch on May clock in anywhere (floater team) for a relief or floater team.

The workers in that team then see their name on every Clock Point, even if they are linked to a specific site themselves.

actions.label: External workers
actions.text:
Switch on External worker for someone who works for another company. For example an installer, a painter or a self-employed person.

You can then enter a company name, for example Elektro Peeters.

In the list you recognise this person by the Ext badge, possibly together with the company name.

An external worker signs in in the same way as an internal worker. There is no separate portal and no separate login.

actions.label: Documents and announcements
actions.text:
Within a team you can make documents and announcements available to the workers.

They do not appear on a unit’s QR page. They also do not count towards your organisation’s document limit.

actions.label: Who is the content for?
actions.text:
For each document or announcement you choose who may see it:
• The whole team.
• One specific worker.

A contract, for example, is meant for one person.

Tick Active to show the document or announcement on Clock Point.

actions.label: What happens when someone changes team?
actions.text:
• A document or announcement for one worker moves with that person when they go to another team.
• A document or announcement for the whole team stays with that team.

actions.label: What does the worker see?
actions.text:
On Clock Point a worker only sees the content that is meant for them.

New content appears straight away under the sign-in card, with a blue counter. When the worker opens the tile, it moves back down. When new content arrives, the tile appears at the top again.

actions.label: Managing and searching
actions.text:
On the team page you see the active documents and announcements by default, 25 per page.

You can filter by:
• Worker.
• Status.
• Search term.

Next to a worker you see a counter. Tap it to open Manage documents or Manage announcements. You then reach that team’s list, filtered on that person.

actions.label: Who opened the content?
actions.text:
For each item you see, for example, Opened 3/5. Tap it to see who has already opened the content and who has not.

WinProx does not store a date or time for this.

An item counts as opened when:
• A document: the worker downloads it.
• An announcement: the worker opens the Announcements screen.

If you replace a document or change an announcement, everyone has to open the new content again.

actions.label: Home group on the roster
actions.text:
This feature is optional.

On Time → Roster you can filter by a location. The workers then appear under groups, for example G1.

You create those groups on a unit via Locations → edit unit → Roster code.

For the worker you then choose which group that person belongs to. Leave this field empty if you do not need groups.

This does not plan shifts. You fill in the label in a roster cell, such as D1 or G1, separately.

actions.label: Print briefing
actions.text:
With Print briefing you open a printable overview of the open tasks per team.

Useful to use on the work floor.

You will find the same briefing on Home, under Issues and on the Calendar.

actions.label: Order of the teams
actions.text:
With Sort order you decide the order in which teams appear in lists and drop-down lists.

A lower number appears higher in the list.

actions.label: Breaks and long shifts
actions.text: For each team you can set a minimum break, for example 30 minutes.

actions.label: Minimum break
actions.text:
Does a worker clock out, or does WinProx close the shift automatically, and does that shift last at least 4 hours? Then WinProx takes the set minimum break into account on the timesheet.

Was less break clocked than the minimum, or no break at all? Then WinProx fills the difference.

This is not a break recorded on Clock Point, and it does not affect the CIAO record.

Via Time → Clocked hours an administrator can also apply the minimum manually or change the break minutes.

actions.label: Alert and automatic close
actions.text:
For each team you also set two time limits. Both are counted from the moment of clocking in.
• Long shift alert: after how many hours the alert appears. Default 10 hours, maximum 24 hours.
• Auto-close: after how many hours an open shift is closed automatically. Default 16 hours, maximum 24 hours.

actions.label: Deactivate a team or a worker
actions.text: You can switch a team or a worker off for a while. Deleting a worker is permanent.

actions.label: Deactivate a team
actions.text:
If you deactivate a team, it disappears from the drop-down lists.

The workers in that team can no longer view or complete tasks. You can activate the team again later.

actions.label: Deactivate a worker
actions.text:
If you deactivate a worker via Edit, that person can no longer sign in on Clock Point.

The details are kept. You can activate the worker again later.

actions.label: Delete a worker
actions.text:
Deleting is permanent.

The history and existing tasks remain, but you can no longer use that worker.

actions.label: Import workers
actions.text: You can add several workers at once with a CSV or Excel file.

actions.label: Required columns
actions.text:
These three columns must be present:
• team_name
• first_name
• last_name

actions.label: Optional columns
actions.text:
You can also include these details:
• email
• phone
• company_name
• location_names

In location_names you enter the site names, separated by commas.

If you leave this field empty, the worker may clock in anywhere.

If you enter a company name in company_name, the worker is created as external automatically.

actions.label: What happens during the import?
actions.text:
Does a team not exist yet? Then WinProx creates it automatically.

Is a column name wrong, or is a required name missing? Then nothing is imported. WinProx shows what is wrong for each row.

actions.label: Undo an import
actions.text:
After an import you can view the last 10 imports from the past 30 days.

For each import you see:
• The file name.
• The date.
• The number of imported workers.

With Undo import you remove the workers from that import who do not yet have a linked phone.

Workers who have already signed in on Clock Point are kept. You recognise them by Has devices.

The Undo import button disappears once every worker from that import who could still be removed has been removed.

actions.label: What is the photo album for?
actions.text:
With the photo album, workers can take photos of a unit via the QR code. You can then select these photos and send them to someone by email.

For example in a nursery: carers take photos of the children during childcare. You can then forward the selected photos to the parents.

The photos are linked to the unit where they were taken. That way you can find them easily.

actions.label: Turn the photo album on or off
actions.text:
The photo album is available for the whole organisation.

The administrator can switch the feature on under Settings → Your organisation.

Is the photo album off? Then the feature is not visible anywhere:
• Not on a unit’s QR page.
• Not in the WinProx menu.

actions.label: Taking photos
actions.text:
A signed-in worker scans a unit’s QR code and opens Photo album.

The photos taken are linked to that unit automatically. The location and the name of the unit are kept with the photos.

Important: these are photos you can email later. They are not used as the unit’s fixed photos or images.

How does it work?
• The phone shrinks the photos automatically before they are saved.
• Up to 24 photos a day can be taken for each unit.
• Each photo shows the date, the time, the worker’s name, the unit and the organisation name.
• A worker can delete their own photos from today.

Before it is saved you can crop the photo to a rectangle.

actions.label: Emailing photos
actions.text:
You manage the photo album via Places → Units → Photo album.

How do you send photos?
1. Choose the unit.
2. Select the day the photos were taken.
3. Tick the photos you want to send.
4. Enter the recipient’s email address.
5. Add a description if you wish, for example Mum of Lotte.
6. Send the photos.

actions.label: Saving email addresses
actions.text:
The email address is saved for that unit. You can select it again easily the next time you send.

You can change the description later or remove the email address.

actions.label: Sending several photos
actions.text:
Each email can include up to 8 photos.

Do you select more than 8 photos? WinProx then splits them automatically across several emails.

The photos are included directly in the email as attachments. The recipient does not need to open a separate download link.

Please note: has a recipient unsubscribed from WinProx emails? Then no photos are sent to that email address.

actions.label: Keeping and deleting photos
actions.text:
Photos are deleted automatically after 7 days. The photo album stays clear, and photos are not kept longer than needed.

You can also delete photos yourself when they are no longer needed.

actions.label: Following up sends
actions.text:
Under Sends you will find an overview of emails that have been sent and emails that are scheduled.

For each send you can see whether the email:
• Has been sent.
• Is still waiting to be sent.
• Could not be sent.

That way you can easily check whether the photos were sent to the recipient.

actions.label: What do you find on this screen?
actions.text:
Here you set up WinProx to match how your organisation works and what it needs.

You manage the organisation details, the available features, punch clock security and how WinProx looks.

Not everyone sees the same settings:
• Administrators can change the settings for the whole organisation.
• Employees can set their own email notifications and personal WinProx style.
• Time users get extra settings for the punch clock, the roster and presence reporting to the NSSO (CIAO).

actions.label: Configuration overview
actions.text:
At the top you find Configuration overview. It is collapsed by default.

Is there a number next to it? Then there are still action items that need attention.

Open the overview to see how far your organisation is with the setup. You also find counts, such as inactive locations, units, teams and workers.

For the main action items you can click Fix straight away.

Want to see everything? Choose Open full overview. You go to a separate page with every item that still needs attention.

actions.label: Your organisation
actions.text: Here you find the settings and details that belong to your organisation.

actions.label: Organisation details
actions.text:
You see the name, email address, phone number and address of your organisation.

As an administrator you change these details with Edit organisation details.

The details are used on printed QR codes, among other places.

actions.label: Organisation logo
actions.text:
Upload your organisation logo as a PNG or JPG file of at most 2 MB.

The logo appears on the WinProx portal and on the QR codes.

As an employee you can only view the logo. Only an administrator can change it.

actions.label: Photo album
actions.text:
Only an administrator can turn the photo album on or off. The setting applies immediately.

• On: workers can take photos via the QR code of a unit. In Photo album you can then email those photos to an address. The files are deleted automatically after one week.
• Off: the photo feature is not available.

actions.label: Email notifications
actions.text:
This is a personal setting. Each user decides whether they want to receive emails.

Turn on Receive an email for every new report if you also want an email for every new report via a QR code.

The setting applies immediately.

Employees can change this preference themselves too.

actions.label: Work menu settings
actions.text:
Only administrators can choose which items appear under Work in the menu.

That keeps the menu clear and shows only the features your organisation uses.

Turn the items you want on or off, then click Confirm.

These are the available settings:
• Issues & tasks: this is the main switch for issues and tasks. If you turn it off, issues and tasks disappear from the menu, the home screen and the workers’ portal. The other switches below are then no longer available.
• Inspection rounds: turn the list and planning of inspection rounds on or off. Unit checks stay available separately.
• Checklists: choose whether you want to use checklist templates in the backoffice. Unit checks stay available separately.
• Unit checks: manage unit check results and checks via the QR code. If you turn this off, unit checks via QR codes also stop on units where this was turned on before.
• Calendar: turn on the calendar for tasks, issues and reservations.
• Reservations: turn reservation management in WinProx on or off. Reservations that were already available on existing units keep working via the QR code. You cannot turn on new reservations on a unit while this setting is off.
• Unit measurements: manage the measure fields and the history of measurements. Measurements via QR codes keep working on units where they were already on. You cannot turn on new measurements while this setting is off.

actions.label: Customers on location
actions.text:
Only administrators can set this.

Does your organisation work at customer sites, for example with cleaning or construction crews? Then turn on Works with customers on location.

For organisations that only work at their own sites, such as a daycare or an office, leave this off.

• On: Customers appears in the menu. You can then link your locations to customers.
• Off: the item disappears from the menu. Customer details that were already created are kept.

Click Save to keep your choice.

actions.label: Punch clock security
actions.text:
This section appears only when Time is on.

Here you choose how workers sign in and how the punch clock is secured.

Each worker clocks in with their own phone. Another device is refused until you or a team leader allows that new device.

Most security options are off by default. Turn on only what your organisation needs.

actions.label: General settings
actions.text:
• Clock in from back office: administrators and employees who belong to a punch clock team can clock themselves in from the sidebar. They sign in with their email address and password.
• Allow external workers: you can mark a worker as an external person. You can also enter the company name.
• Team roster visible to workers: this setting appears only when the roster is on. Workers can then see the roster of colleagues at their locations on their phone.
• Require a 4-digit PIN when signing in at Clock Point: workers must enter a personal PIN when signing in at a Clock Point, instead of only choosing their icon. The icon still applies to the QR code of a unit.
• Sign in with fingerprint or face (passkey): workers can sign in with the security of their phone, for example a fingerprint or face recognition. Signing in with a PIN or icon remains possible.
• Evacuation list on Clock Point: after signing in, workers can open the evacuation list. Before they open it, they must confirm that the view is exceptional. Each view is recorded.

actions.label: Working on location (GPS)
actions.text:
Does your organisation work at customers on different sites? Then you can set the GPS check here.

These settings are not needed when everyone clocks in at a fixed punch clock in the same building.

• Ask for GPS when clocking in or out: when clocking in, the phone must share a location. If that fails, the worker cannot clock in. Clocking out remains possible.
• GPS work visits (start/stop work on a location or unit pin): workers can start and stop their work visit at a customer. The phone must be within the set distance of the work address.
• Radius (metres): how close the worker must be to the work address. The default is 50 metres.

Click Save punch clock security to keep your changes.

actions.label: Roster
actions.text:
This setting is in a separate section under Punch clock security.

Turn off Use the roster if your organisation does not plan in WinProx.

These items then disappear from the menu:
• Roster.
• Shift types.
• Public holidays.
• Minimum staffing.
• Requests.

Good to know: the other features keep working. Signing in via QR, tasks and the punch clock stay available. Shifts that were already created are not deleted. They are kept.

Click Save to confirm your choice.

actions.label: Customise WinProx style
actions.text:
Here you choose how WinProx looks when you work in the Backoffice.

Your choice applies on every device where you are signed in, and it applies immediately.

You can choose from three styles:
• Modern: the default style, with a dark menu bar and cards with a glass look.
• Standard: a light, calm look without a background photo.
• Dark: a fully dark look.

As an administrator you can also change the background and the portal colours below.

actions.label: Background
actions.text:
At Apply to you choose where to use the image.

There are two options:
• Portal background: the background someone sees after scanning a QR code. This is not the background of the QR sticker itself.
• Backoffice background: the image behind the backoffice screen. It is visible in the Modern style.

You can choose a standard background or upload your own image.

Your choice is saved immediately. If you upload your own image, it replaces the standard background.

The remove button takes you back to the standard background.

actions.label: Portal colours
actions.text:
Here you choose the background colour and the button colour of the reporting portal.

On the right you see a preview of the screen for someone who scans a QR code and wants to send a report.

These colours do not change how the Backoffice looks.

Click Save to keep your colour choice.

actions.label: QR print sheet
actions.text:
Here you choose how the QR stickers and print sheets for your organisation look.

You can change the design and then download print sheets per location.

Click Save to keep the text, the logo and the address. A custom background is saved immediately.

actions.label: Text on the sticker
actions.text:
At the top of the sticker you can place your own text of at most 120 characters.

Leave this field empty? Then WinProx uses the location name and the unit.

Under the QR code the unique sticker number is always shown.

actions.label: Logo and address
actions.text:
You choose where the organisation logo and the address appear on the sticker.

For both you can choose from four corners:
• Bottom right.
• Bottom left.
• Top right.
• Top left.

You can also choose Do not show if you prefer to leave out the logo or the address.

The logo in the centre of the QR code always stays. You cannot move it here.

actions.label: Background
actions.text:
You can use a standard background or upload your own image.

Your own background must be a PNG or JPG file of at most 4 MB.

Without your own image, WinProx uses the standard design.

Want to use the standard design again? Click Remove custom background.

actions.label: Preview
actions.text:
On the right you see a preview of one sticker with your chosen settings.

When you open a print sheet from a location, the real QR codes and sticker numbers of that location are used.

That way you see in advance how your stickers will look.

actions.label: NSSO presence (CIAO)
actions.text:
You find this section at the bottom of the settings, just above Privacy. It is collapsed by default.

You cannot turn CIAO on yourself.

Do you want to use presence reporting to the NSSO? Request activation via info@winprox.app.

WinProx then turns the feature on for your organisation.

actions.label: Set up CIAO
actions.text:
After activation you fill in your enterprise number (CBE).

Does your organisation not have a Belgian enterprise number? Then fill in the foreign VAT number.

If the field Regime appears, choose the regime that applies:
• Cleaning (CIAO).
• Construction / concrete (CIAO).

Click Save CIAO settings to keep your details.

With All CIAO submissions you open the overview of the presence reports that were sent to the NSSO.

actions.label: Privacy & data export
actions.text:
This section is only available to administrators.

With Download data export you can download a file with your organisation’s details and the relevant activity in WinProx.

The export can also contain sensitive information.

Keep the file in a safe place and share it only with people who may access these details.

actions.label: What is this page?
actions.text: Here you connect WinProx to other software — for example your ERP, a planning tool or a custom dashboard. WinProx then talks to that system digitally, so you do not have to retype issues manually.

actions.label: Do I need this?
actions.text:
Usually not. If you only use WinProx via the website and QR codes, you do not need to configure anything here.

For one-off setup: Want to import thousands of units or workers at once? Use the CSV/Excel import on a location (units) or on Teams (workers). That is often faster and simpler for an initial migration.

For ongoing automation: This API page is intended for administrators or IT partners who want to build a live integration so systems communicate automatically (e.g. real-time ERP connections or custom dashboards).

actions.label: API — what is it?
actions.text: An API lets other programs read WinProx data or perform actions (e.g. list issues and tasks). This works securely with an API token — like a password used by software, not by people.

actions.label: Creating an API token
actions.text: Give the token a clear name (e.g. "ERP integration"). After creation you see the code once: copy and store it immediately. WinProx will not show it again. If you lose it, create a new token and revoke the old one.

actions.label: Revoking a token
actions.text: No longer using an integration, or worried a token was exposed? Click Revoke. That integration stops working. Other tokens stay active.

actions.label: What can the API do?
actions.text: With a valid token, software can among other things read issues and tasks, list locations/units/teams/workers, create or approve issues, and start or complete tasks. For technical docs, ask your IT partner or WinProx support.

actions.label: Webhooks — what are they?
actions.text: A webhook is the opposite of the API: WinProx sends a message to your system when something happens (e.g. new issue or task completed). You provide a URL where WinProx may post data.

actions.label: Adding a webhook endpoint
actions.text: Enter a full URL starting with https:// (secure connection). Tick the events you want to receive. Optionally add a description (e.g. "Production ERP"). Save — WinProx stores the address and sends data automatically for those events.

actions.label: Event: issue.created
actions.text: A new issue was received (via QR, manually or via the API). Useful to create a ticket in an external system right away.

actions.label: Event: issue.approved
actions.text: An administrator approved an issue (often from QR). Only then is the content also visible on public QR pages.

actions.label: Event: issue.status_changed
actions.text: An issue's status changed (e.g. from open to in progress), usually because tasks were started or completed.

actions.label: Event: task.created
actions.text: A new task was created for a team, linked to an issue.

actions.label: Event: task.started
actions.text: A worker started a task via the field portal (unit QR).

actions.label: Event: task.completed
actions.text: A task was completed by the team. Useful to update external systems or reports.

actions.label: Event: unit.gps_reported
actions.text: A GPS location was recorded for a unit via the portal (reporter, worker or admin during QR linking). Payload includes coordinates and optionally location_name and country_code (GeoNames).

actions.label: Endpoint active or inactive
actions.text: Temporarily turn off an endpoint without deleting it (e.g. during server maintenance). Inactive endpoints receive no messages.

actions.label: Recent deliveries
actions.text: Log of the latest webhook attempts. "success" means your system received the message. "failed" means something went wrong (wrong URL, server offline, …). Shows delivery status only — not issue content.

actions.label: Security
actions.text: Treat API tokens like passwords: do not share them in email or chat. Webhooks are cryptographically signed so your server can verify the message really came from WinProx — your IT partner can implement this check.

actions.label: Help with the integration
actions.text: Not sure if something works? Ask your IT partner to check the URL, events and recent deliveries. For WinProx itself, use Contact or the FAQ if you do not have a developer.

actions.label: What do you see on this screen?
actions.text:
Here you find all information about your WinProx subscription.

Among other things, you see:
• Whether your organisation is still in the trial period.
• Which plan is currently active.
• Until when your subscription runs.
• Which limits belong to your plan, such as the number of licences, units and documents.

actions.label: What is a licence?
actions.text:
A licence is for one person who uses WinProx. That can be someone who works in the Backoffice, or a worker on the floor.

Does the same person use both? Then that person still counts as one licence. You do not pay twice.

actions.label: Trial period
actions.text:
During the trial period you can try WinProx with the same limits as the smallest WinProx plan.

You have:
• Up to 5 licences.
• Up to 50 units.
• Up to 10 documents.

Time, including the punch clock, is included. IoT, ESG and API are not available during the trial.

On the home screen and on this page you see how many days your trial still lasts.

actions.label: After the trial
actions.text:
Want to keep using WinProx? Choose a plan in time.

If the trial ends without a subscription, you first receive warning emails. If no subscription is activated, your organisation may later be removed automatically.

actions.label: Choose a WinProx plan
actions.text:
WinProx offers standard plans for 5, 10, 25 or 50 licences.

You choose which plan fits your organisation best. Payment is monthly via Stripe.

How many units and documents you get depends on the plan you choose. Locations and photos are unlimited.

Included in the standard plans:
• Punch clock and time recording.
• Roster.
• CIAO (NSSO), when you want to use it.

Not included:
• IoT.
• ESG.
• API and webhooks.

Those options are available in Corporate.

Tip: need more than 50 licences, or want to connect your own software via API or webhooks? Then Corporate may be the right choice.

actions.label: Corporate
actions.text:
Corporate is for larger organisations or organisations that need extra options.

This plan is available from about 100 licences, but can also make sense when you need API or webhooks.

Depending on your agreement, the following can be included:
• Time.
• IoT.
• ESG.
• API and webhooks.

Price and available limits are agreed with you.

Is your organisation on Corporate? Then you cannot switch to another plan yourself from this screen. Only a Superuser can do that.

Here you do see the number of units agreed for your organisation.

More information or a proposal? Contact us at info@winprox.app.

actions.label: CIAO (NSSO)
actions.text:
CIAO is the presence declaration to the NSSO (National Social Security Office).

Want to use it? Request activation via info@winprox.app.

A Superuser then activates the feature for your organisation.

Good to know: you do not need a Corporate subscription for CIAO. Time is activated with it.

actions.label: Checkmate
actions.text:
Checkmate is the simple WinProx plan for crews that work at different customer sites — cleaning companies, for example.

Workers use their phone to clock in and out. At each customer they start a visit. WinProx checks via the phone location whether the worker is really at the work address, within a radius of 100 m.

What is included?
• Customers and work addresses: manage the customers and places where your workers work.
• Punch clock: workers clock in and out, including breaks.
• Own hours: each worker can view their worked hours.
• Hours per customer: as an admin you see how much time was worked at each customer.
• CIAO (NSSO): the presence declaration to the NSSO is included. Enter your CBE number under Settings for that.

What is not included?
• Reports.
• Tasks.
• Units.
• Documents.
• Roster.

Price
You pay €5 per active licence per month. That can be a colleague or a worker.

You choose how many active licences you need.

Expand later?
Does your organisation need more options later? Then you can move to a regular WinProx plan.

Your existing data is kept. You do not have to start again.

actions.label: Delete your organisation and data
actions.text:
Want to stop WinProx and remove your whole organisation? Only an admin can do that.

Step 1 — Download your data first
Export your data beforehand via:
Settings → Privacy & data export

That way you still have your data when you no longer use WinProx.

Step 2 — Request deletion
Go to Subscription and:
1. Tick the confirmation for deletion.
2. Enter your password.
3. Confirm your request.

All admins of the organisation then receive a confirmation email.

What happens next?
What follows depends on your subscription.

• During the trial: after the request you can carry out the final deletion yourself.
• On a paid subscription: there is first a waiting period of 7 days. During that period a warning appears on screen and you receive a reminder email. WinProx administration then carries out the final deletion.

During processing WinProx keeps a technical snapshot without media files for 30 days.

Changed your mind? You can cancel the request during the waiting period via Subscription.

Important: always download your data before you confirm deletion. After final deletion you can no longer consult your organisation data via WinProx.

actions.label: Version history
actions.text: Here you see only what changed in the last week, newest day first. Each day is grouped under New, Improved, Fixed or Important. Older days are kept, but they are not shown on this page.

actions.label: Knowledge base
actions.text: Answers to frequently asked questions about WinProx, QR, teams, Time, ESG, portal approval/blur, and page help (?).

actions.label: Support
actions.text: Contact WinProx if you need help beyond this page help and the FAQ.

portal.worker.qr.title: Help — QR codes on the shop floor

actions.label: Unit QR
actions.text: Attached to a machine, room or asset. Citizens can report issues here. As a worker, sign in first on the Clock Point portal; then scan the unit QR to start or complete open tasks on that unit. When unit checks are enabled, signed-in workers can also record OK/Not OK (with an optional checklist).

actions.label: Clock Point QR
actions.text: Placed at the entrance, warehouse or workshop — as a sticker or as a clock screen with a rotating QR. Workers sign in here (name + icon); the sign-in link or the home screen icon works too. Clocking in/out requires Time (punch clock) and, on a fixed punch clock, a fresh scan each time (with Checkmate the icon is enough). With GPS work visits they can complete team tasks and the next inspection stop (unit check) on Clock Point.

portal.unit.title: Help — Public portal

actions.label: Welcome
actions.text: Welcome to the public portal of :tenant. Read below for more information. Interested in your own company portal? Click on Winprox.app.

actions.label: Report issue
actions.text: Tap "Create report", describe the problem and optionally add up to four photos. First name, last name and email are optional — unless the administrator made contact details required; then fill them in. If email confirmation is on, you receive a link: the report is only created after you confirm it. A task is then created for the team. The report must be approved before it appears on the portal. Anti-spam limits apply: at most one report per 3 minutes and five reports per 30 minutes for this unit (per device).

actions.label: Previous reports
actions.text: If the administrator leaves this on for the category, you see open reports for this unit after approval. If it is off, that tile is hidden (for example a hotel room or restroom).

actions.label: Reserve
actions.text: If this unit is reservable, you see the Reserve tile. Pick a time slot, enter name and email, and confirm within 30 minutes via email. Use My reservations or the mail link to change or cancel.

actions.label: Documents
actions.text: View the manuals and other documents available for this unit here. The description is translated automatically into Dutch, English, French, German, Spanish and Italian, once ready. Portuguese, Romanian and Polish are extra screen languages of the portal; the organisation’s text then stays in the language it was written in.

actions.label: Announcements
actions.text: View the announcements that apply specifically to this unit here. The text is translated automatically into Dutch, English, French, German, Spanish and Italian, once ready. Portuguese, Romanian and Polish are extra screen languages of the portal; the organisation’s text then stays in the language it was written in.

actions.label: Capture GPS location
actions.text: When enabled, your GPS coordinates are shared with the administration. This helps a technician find you easily.

actions.label: Language
actions.text: Choose the language in the top right. The back office and website use Dutch, English, French, German, Spanish and Italian. This portal also offers Portuguese, Romanian and Polish; more languages can be added here later. The screen texts follow the chosen language at once.

actions.label: Theme
actions.text: Switch between Standard and Dark themes in the top right for a view that matches your preference. Dark is useful on mobile.

actions.label: Unit measurements
actions.text: When category and unit allow unit measurements and fields are linked, the portal shows the Measure tile. Enter values and submit — Clock Point not required. History under Work → Unit measurements.

actions.label: Photo album
actions.text: When the photo album is on, it sits with the photo cards on this unit QR. Those are today's photos to email, not the unit's permanent photos. Up to 24 a day; you can delete your own photos from today. The back office decides what is sent.

portal.unit.status_note: Open tasks on this page follow the statuses below.

actions.label: Add photos
actions.text: When starting or completing a task, add photos as proof or explanation. Photos are automatically compressed for fast upload.

actions.label: Wait for upload
actions.text: Wait until the upload finishes before confirming — otherwise photos will be missing from the task.

portal.team.title: Help — Worker portal

actions.label: Name and icon
actions.text: After opening the Clock Point portal — via a QR scan, the sign-in link or the home screen icon — enter your first and last name and choose a personal icon. Remember this icon well, because next time you must select it again. You get two attempts to sign in with the correct icon; after that your account is blocked. A team leader or administrator can unblock your account in that case.

actions.label: First time
actions.text: New to the team? Ask your team leader or administrator to create an account for you. After that you can sign in with your first and last name and choose your own icon.

actions.label: Sign out
actions.text: Sign out when you are finished. At times set by the administrator you are also automatically signed out.

actions.label: Open tasks
actions.text: After signing in you see open tasks for your team on the unit portal. Scan the unit QR on site to start or complete a task.

actions.label: New team tasks
actions.text: If new tasks for your team arrived since you signed in, the unit portal shows a sticky attention banner. Open the task overview via the Clock Point link or dismiss the banner.

actions.label: Start
actions.text: Go to "Open tasks" and click on "Start task". Other team members will then see that you are working on this task and the status changes to "In progress". Once you are finished, click on "Complete task". Without coverage the start is saved on the device and sent later.

actions.label: Complete
actions.text: After you have started the task, complete it by clicking on "Complete task". Here you can add a short note and optionally attach photos. Sometimes the portal asks for a measurement value (e.g. a meter reading) — enter it before you confirm. The task then gets status "Completed". Without coverage the note and photos stay on the device until you are back online.

actions.label: Unit check
