actions.text: When category and unit both allow unit checks, signed-in workers see the Unit check tile. Record OK or Not OK, optionally with a checklist. OK does not create an issue; after Not OK you can create a report. Without coverage the check is saved on the device and sent later.

actions.label: Capture GPS location
actions.text: When enabled, your GPS coordinates are shared with the administration. This helps a technician find you easily.

portal.team.status_note: Each task goes through the statuses below:

statuses.new: The task is not yet started and waiting for a worker.
statuses.in_progress: Someone is currently working on the task on site.
statuses.done: The work has been completed by a worker.
statuses.closed: The issue has been checked by the administrator and definitively closed.

actions.label: Role
actions.text: A team leader is a worker with extra rights on the team portal. You handle tasks yourself and help colleagues get started.

actions.label: Assignment
actions.text: An administrator assigns team leaders in WinProx on the team. You see the «Team leader» badge after signing in.

actions.label: Clock Point QR
actions.text: Scan the Clock Point QR and sign in with your name and icon — the same as any worker.

actions.label: Extra panels
actions.text: After signing in you see extra sections: release colleague icon and manage workers (including taking photos).

actions.label: When needed
actions.text: If a colleague picked the wrong icon too often, they are blocked. You can release the icon so they can choose again.

actions.label: Steps
actions.text: Open «Release», confirm your own icon first, select the blocked colleague and confirm. The colleague can then sign in again.

actions.label: Overview
actions.text: Open «Manage» to see the workers of your team, to add one, or to take or update a photo.

actions.label: Add
actions.text: Add a new worker with first and last name. Then let the colleague scan the Clock Point QR to register and choose an icon.

actions.label: Remove
actions.text: Only remove a worker you just created yourself (within 24 hours). Other team members are removed by the administrator. You cannot remove yourself.

actions.label: Photo
actions.text: Click a colleague's photo to take or choose a photo. The photo is cropped on the phone and then visible in the back office. Click the cross to remove the photo.

portal.teamleader.tasks.title: Help — Handle tasks

actions.label: Same as worker
actions.text: Start open tasks, add notes, attach photos and complete — identical to the workers manual.

actions.label: Coordination
actions.text: Keep overview of open tasks and coordinate who picks up which task with your team.

portal.teamleader.tasks.status_note: Task statuses are the same as for all workers.

statuses.done: Completed by you or a colleague.

actions.label: Name and icon
actions.text: Open the Clock Point portal by scanning the sticker or the clock screen, via the sign-in link from an email or via the home screen icon, and choose your first and last name plus your personal icon (optional PIN or biometrics) on your own phone. That is who you are — it is not clocking in yet. There is no button to sign in as a different worker: the phone stays yours until an admin or team leader releases it. After sign-in the Sign in heading disappears. Two wrong attempts temporarily block your account; a team leader or administrator can release it.

actions.label: Fingerprint or face
actions.text: After your first sign-in with icon or PIN, the portal offers «Faster sign-in?» — tap Enable and confirm with your phone’s fingerprint or face (or device code). From then on the Sign in with biometrics button sits on top; icon or PIN always still works. Your fingerprint or face never leaves your phone — WinProx only stores a public key. No offer? Then your admin has disabled the option or your device does not support it. Admins can remove your passkey via People → Teams → Edit.

actions.label: Home screen shortcut
actions.text: A WinProx icon sits to the right of Sign in. Tap: on Android Chrome adds it to the home screen; on iPhone: ⋯ at the bottom → Share → Show more → scroll down → + Add to Home Screen. No App Store. That icon signs you in without a QR; on a fixed punch clock you can only clock in or out after scanning the sticker or the clock screen.

actions.label: Push notifications
actions.text: Put WinProx on the home screen first, using the logo with the plus. Then open that icon. The button Turn on push notifications is only inside that app. Tap it and allow notifications. The button disappears at once; you do not need to refresh the page. You then get an alert when your shift changes, leave or time off is approved, a document or announcement is ready, or you are still clocked in after your shift. Also for a new task for you or your team, once each morning for your recurring tasks, and when leave or time off is declined. On an iPhone this only works when you open WinProx from the home screen icon. Only on this phone. The alert does not include text from the document.

actions.label: Sign out
actions.text: After sign-in you can Sign out: the portal then asks for your icon, PIN or biometrics again. That is not clock-out and does not unbind the phone; only an admin or team leader releases the device. Clock-out is on your clock-in line.

actions.label: Open tasks
actions.text: After name and icon you see the clock card at the top with your status (not clocked in, clocked in, on break, another site, or leave). The place sits underneath, and the main action sits next to your name. Start break and Sign out are buttons behind the arrow. Open tasks sit below, with a count; extra tasks via More tasks. With Time + GPS work visits you start or complete team tasks on Clock Point while an open work visit is on that customer location (optional note and photos). An inspection round shows description, priority, status and the next stop. The Unit check button appears only after Start work at that location; the full check (OK / Not OK / skip) opens after that.

actions.label: Clock in and out
actions.text: Each clock-in, clock-out or move needs a fresh scan of the sticker or the clock screen on site — the sign-in link, the home screen icon or an open tab is not enough (with Checkmate the icon does work). One scan gives one punch and expires quickly. You can start breaks on the same phone without a new scan. If the GPS-on-clock-in setting is on, your location is required to clock in; clock-out and breaks need no position. Another device is refused until a team leader or admin allows a new device. You have one open shift at a time. At a Clock Point of another site you see where you are clocked in and can move presence here (a hop within 5 minutes raises an alarm). Another Clock Point on the same site counts as the same place. With GPS work visits: start work on site, then team tasks and the next inspection stop on Clock Point. A red triangle next to the clock-in time appears when you have a published shift and have not clocked in, or clocked in at least 15 minutes late.

actions.label: Clock screen
actions.text: If a clock screen hangs at the punch clock, the QR on that screen keeps refreshing — scanning it with your phone counts as a fresh scan. No phone at hand? Tap your name on the screen; on an open shift choose break or clock-out, then your PIN. Two wrong attempts block that briefly. Without a PIN you clock in via a scan on your phone.

actions.label: Where do I need to go today
actions.text: After clock-in (Time with GPS work visits) you see where you need to go today: locations only, in inspection-round stop order (not alphabetical), as a timeline (here, next, been, later). The next stop shows the address and Navigate. If GPS is off on your phone you see a warning — only when you have somewhere to go today. Start work appears at the location when you are on site; Find a nearby workplace then disappears. Inspection stops are under Open tasks; Unit check only after Start work. Open tasks without a date stay under Open tasks.

actions.label: New documents and announcements
actions.text: New documents and announcements temporarily appear directly under your sign-in card, with a blue counter. Open the tile to view the content; it then returns to its fixed place at the bottom. If new content arrives later, the tile moves up again. Your read state belongs to you and is also retained on another device. A document counts as opened once you download it, announcements once you open the Announcements screen. What you have not opened yet is at the top with New, or Changed if your manager edited it.

actions.label: Evacuation list
actions.text: If an admin turned the evacuation list on in Settings (off by default), you see the Evacuation list tile (fire icon) after sign-in. First confirm that the consultation is exceptional and is logged (first name, last name, date and time). Then you see who is clocked in now, grouped by site, newest clock-in first.

actions.label: My hours
actions.text: After sign-in you see the My hours tile. It lists your days for the selected month, merged: first clock-in, last clock-out, time worked and break. Browse previous/next month. Break shows “none” when there is no break. The team minimum only applies on shifts of at least 4 hours. A red triangle shows the reason: clocked in more than 15 minutes early, clocked in at least 15 minutes late, or clocked out at least 15 minutes late versus the published roster.

actions.label: My roster
actions.text: After signing in you see the My roster tile. It shows only your published shifts and absences for the chosen month, as a table (empty days are skipped). A badge means a newly published roster; opening it clears the badge. A red triangle next to the hours means not clocked in (from the planned start) or at least 15 minutes late.

actions.label: Leave / Absence
actions.text: After sign-in you see the Leave / Absence tile. Choose the absence by name (e.g. Leave, Sick, Personal day) — types come from your organisation’s shift types. The list is Leave, Comp time, Sick, then Other (by name). Then from–to (Other: one day), optional note, max. 31 days, not in the past. Overlapping open requests are refused. Your own requests sit below the form: you can withdraw an open or approved request that has not started; approved leave restores the roster. Staff decide under Time → Requests; reject needs a reason, approve does not. No email is sent. At the top you see leave left this year of the entitlement, and next year when an entitlement is set, plus overtime. This year up to today: time worked minus the published roster, minus time off already on the roster or in an open request. Not pay. You can add a photo of a note, up to four. WinProx keeps it for 6 months and then deletes it. Keep your own copy if you need it longer.

actions.label: What gets translated?
actions.text: Automatic translation slots (NL, EN, FR, DE, ES, IT) for: approved QR issues (description); active announcements (description); active units (name and description); tasks with their own description; active documents (description — title stays in source language). Tasks without their own description show the linked issue translation. Those are the languages of the back office, the website and automatic translation. The worker portal is separate: it also offers Portuguese, Romanian and Polish, and more portal languages can be added later. Those extra languages translate only the screen texts and the help, not the content the organisation writes.

actions.label: Local via Ollama
actions.text: As superuser on your laptop: start php artisan queue:work, click « Start translations ». Pending issues, announcements, units, tasks and documents are exported, translated locally, and imported back on the server.

actions.label: Server status
actions.text: On production you see how many translations are still waiting. The count includes all of these types.

actions.label: Source text changed
actions.text: If someone edits the source text of an announcement, unit, task or document, existing translations are invalidated and set to pending again. Run a new translation sync afterwards.

actions.label: Manage tenants
actions.text: Overview of all organisations. Open a tenant to work in their environment as support.

actions.label: Support mode
actions.text: Start support to use the app on behalf of a tenant. Stop support to return to the platform overview.

actions.label: Modules
actions.text: Turn optional modules on or off (ESG, IoT Connect, CIAO/NSSO). CIAO is exceptional: the organisation requests it via info@winprox.app. A Superuser enables CIAO (Time turns on; Corporate not required). Time is included in WinProx plans.

actions.label: Assign plan
actions.text: Choose the plan (WinProx 5/10/25/50 or Corporate) and assign it. For Corporate: enter the units cap. CIAO can be enabled without Corporate.

actions.label: New password
actions.text: Set a new password for a user of an organisation. No email is sent. Pass the password on yourself. A superuser does not get a new password here.

actions.label: Unanswered questions
actions.text: Questions from the help chat with no FAQ match. Answer them or add them to the knowledge base.

actions.label: Knowledge base
actions.text: Manage FAQ articles and help answers for all tenants.

actions.label: What is this screen?
actions.text: Manage addresses that no longer receive WinProx emails — marketing, contact and system mail. Only superusers see this page.

actions.label: Block an address
actions.text: Add an email address manually to block it. That row gets the source Blocked manually.

actions.label: Search and filter
actions.text: Search by email address. The checkboxes filter on the same source as in the list. Nothing checked shows everything.

actions.label: Unsubscribe source
actions.text: Unsubscribed by recipient = via the unsubscribe link in an email. Undeliverable (bounce) = automatic after an undeliverable promo email. Blocked manually = via this screen.

actions.label: Restore
actions.text: Restore removes the address from the list; it will receive emails again.

actions.label: What is this screen?
actions.text: The ESG dashboard gives an operational overview of your measurement programme: latest values, threshold alarms, trends, and open follow-up actions. It is your starting point for day-to-day ESG management — detail and history are on the Measurements tab.

actions.label: KPI cards at the top
actions.text: The first card shows the number of threshold alarms in the recent sample. You also see the latest reading per active numeric indicator and when it was recorded. Highlighted in red = outside minimum or maximum. Click a card to open the filtered measurements overview.

actions.label: Usage trend
actions.text: Line chart for the selected indicator over the last 30 days. Readings per day are summed (useful for consumption indicators such as kWh). Choose another indicator at the top right to compare trends.

actions.label: Readings within limits
actions.text: The donut shows the percentage of recent readings (sample) that fall within the configured thresholds. The caption below states how many alarms are in that sample. Click to open the measurements overview.

actions.label: Highest usage per location
actions.text: Ranking of locations by the total sum of readings for the selected indicator in the last 30 days. Useful to see which building or site contributes most. Click a row for readings at that location.

actions.label: ESG score (compliance)
actions.text: Weighted score over the last 30 days: 60% threshold compliance (readings with thresholds that are within limits) + 40% measurement coverage (active numeric indicators with at least one reading). Below the donut you see the individual percentages.

actions.label: Distribution by category
actions.text: Donut of the number of readings per indicator category (e.g. energy, waste, safety) in the last 30 days. Set categories when creating or editing an indicator under Indicators.

actions.label: Open ESG tasks
actions.text: Tasks linked to an ESG indicator that are not yet completed — both periodic measurement tasks and automatic follow-up actions. The Auto-alarm badge marks tasks WinProx created after a threshold breach.

actions.label: Auto-alarm and follow-up task
actions.text: When a reading falls outside the configured minimum or maximum, WinProx can automatically create a priority-2 follow-up task (at most one open task per indicator and unit). The Follow-up task button on recent readings and alarms goes straight to that task. The assigned team follows the team of the original measurement task.

actions.label: Recent readings and threshold alarms
actions.text: Two lists at the bottom: all recent readings, and separately readings with threshold alarms. Values outside limits get the Outside thresholds label. Use Task to open the measurement task from the QR portal.

actions.label: Empty dashboard
actions.text: No indicators or readings yet? WinProx shows getting-started steps: module active, create an indicator, link to a recurring issue. Full guidance on indicators is on the Indicators tab.

actions.label: How does it work?
actions.text: The ESG module lets you collect data systematically on site — energy use, safety checks, waste logging — without asking workers to do anything special. They simply see a task, as usual.

actions.label: Enable module
actions.text: A superuser must first enable the ESG module under Platform → Tenants. Without it, this menu is hidden.

actions.label: Step 1 — Create an indicator
actions.text: An indicator describes what you want to measure: an electricity meter, a fire extinguisher check, or a periodic inspection. Give it a clear name and, for numbers, a unit (e.g. kWh, m³) so it displays correctly at entry.

actions.label: Number
actions.text: For meter readings or counts (e.g. electricity in kWh, water in m³, vehicle mileage). You can set a minimum and maximum so unrealistic entries (e.g. a negative reading) are flagged.

actions.label: Yes/No
actions.text: For quick checks (e.g. "Is the emergency exit clear?", "Is the fire extinguisher inspected?").

actions.label: Text
actions.text: For a short note or comment with a reading (e.g. a remark about an unusual meter value).

actions.label: Choice list
actions.text: For a fixed set of answers (e.g. waste category: General waste, Recyclables, Paper). You define the options when creating the indicator; workers choose from a dropdown on the portal.

actions.label: Linked system
actions.text: When values come in automatically from an external system (via the API). Not intended for manual entry by workers on the QR portal.

actions.label: Step 2 — Link to a recurring issue
actions.text: When creating a recurring issue on a unit, you can link an ESG indicator. From then on, each cycle automatically asks for the corresponding reading — for example the monthly meter reading for that unit.

actions.label: Step 3 — Measurements are stored
actions.text:
Each time a worker completes the task, the entered value is stored with the date and unit. This gradually builds a history per measurement point, useful for reporting (e.g. energy use per building over time).

Once recorded, a measurement cannot be changed — this keeps your data reliable and auditable. The overview is on the Measurements tab.

actions.label: Deactivate indicator
actions.text: No longer using an indicator (e.g. a replaced meter)? Deactivate it instead of deleting. All collected measurements remain fully preserved — you never lose historical data.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: History of all ESG readings on one unit: trend, timeline, and alarms per indicator.

actions.label: Reading and follow-up
actions.text: Under each reading in the timeline you see linked steps: the reading (value), optionally a threshold alarm, the measurement task used to enter the value, and a follow-up task when the value was outside limits. Use Open to jump to the measurements overview or the task.

actions.label: Trend
actions.text: Chart of numeric readings over the recent period for the selected indicator.

actions.label: What do you see here?
actions.text: All readings workers entered when completing a task, with indicator, location, unit, timestamp, and who took the reading. Click Task to view the underlying work item.

actions.label: Filters
actions.text: Narrow by indicator, location, unit, or period. Useful to review all meter readings for one building in a quarter, for example.

actions.label: Download report
actions.text: Export the filtered results (not only the current page; max. 5000 rows): CSV (table for Excel) or Print (same card layout as the backoffice list; Ctrl+P to PDF). Uses the same filters as the list.

actions.label: Threshold warnings
actions.text: If an indicator has a minimum or maximum set, readings outside those limits are highlighted so you spot deviations quickly.

actions.label: External integration
actions.text: Readings can also arrive automatically via an API connection (Settings → API). This is optional — most organisations collect data through the unit QR portal.

actions.label: What do you find on this screen?
actions.text:
Here you see at a glance who is working now and who is not clocked in. The overview updates by itself. You do not need to refresh the page.

At the top you find five tiles:
• Clocked in: everyone with an open shift. These are the workers who are working and those who are on a break.
• Active: workers who are clocked in and are not on a break right now.
• Break: workers who are clocked in and are on a break.
• Not clocked in: active workers who do not have an open shift right now.
• Attention: situations you may need to check. For example someone who has been clocked in for too long, has not taken a break, moved too quickly, clocked in during leave, or viewed the evacuation list. Click this tile to go to Alarms.

Click Active, Break or Not clocked in to see only that group. With Clocked in you return to the full overview of clocked-in workers.

On the presence board you find two columns:
• Present: workers with an open shift.
• Absent / Extra action: workers who are not clocked in, or for whom an extra action may be needed.

For each clocked-in worker you see the name, the team, the clock-in time and the time worked.

If it says Break, the worker is on a break. If it says Working at, that person is at a work address.

An exclamation mark points to something that needs attention. For example when someone clocked in during approved leave.

actions.label: View
actions.text:
Under the filters you choose how you want to see presence.

• Board: a live overview of who is present and who is not clocked in. This is the most useful view for following daily presence.
• Teams: see presence by team. You can open each team to see how many workers are active, on a break or not clocked in.
• Locations: see who is clocked in at each site. With Show teams you also see the teams of that location.

actions.label: Search and filter
actions.text:
With the filters you quickly find the right workers:
• Search worker: search by name.
• Team: choose a specific team, or All teams.
• Location: choose a site, or All locations.
• Clock Point: choose a specific Clock Point, or All clock points.

Do you select a location or Clock Point? Then you only see the workers clocked in there.

Workers who are not clocked in then disappear from the overview. There is no location or Clock Point for them.

actions.label: View a worker’s hours
actions.text:
Do you want to see someone’s clocked hours?

Click the worker’s name. You go straight to Clocked hours, with that person’s details for the last three weeks.

actions.label: Close a shift
actions.text:
Did someone forget to clock out? You can close the open shift yourself.

Click Close shift for that worker.

The shift closes at the current time. You also fill in a reason. That reason is kept with the registration.

Does the team have a set minimum break, and does the shift last at least four hours? Then that break is counted automatically in the hours.

actions.label: Clock in manually
actions.text:
Does a worker not have their phone, or can they not scan the QR code? You can clock that person in yourself.

Click Clock in manually and choose:
• The worker.
• The Clock Point where the person should clock in.
• A reason for the manual registration.

WinProx does not link a device to the worker for this.

After clocking in, the label Clocked in manually appears for that person. You see the same label with the clocked hours and on the Clock Point.

Clocking out happens later with a new QR scan, or you close the shift yourself with Close shift.

actions.label: How do workers clock in and out?
actions.text:
Workers use the QR code of a Clock Point for this.

They scan the code with their phone and then choose their name and icon. Depending on your settings, they also enter a PIN or passkey.

A separate account for the punch clock is not needed.

Important: every clock-in or clock-out needs a new QR scan. A browser page that was already open, or the shortcut on the home screen, is not enough. The worker must scan the QR code on site again each time.

actions.label: Evacuation list
actions.text:
With the evacuation list you can see, in an emergency, who may be present in your organisation.

This feature is off by default. You turn it on via:

Settings → Punch clock security → Evacuation list on Clock Point.

After signing in at a Clock Point, workers then see the tile Evacuation list.

Before they can open the list, they must confirm that they are doing this exceptionally.

Each view is recorded with the first name, last name, date and time.

A view from today appears automatically under Attention. The full history, including views from earlier days, is in Alarms.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: Shows everything that needs attention: clocked in too long, forgotten clock-out, no break recorded, a too-quick hop between Clock Points, or an evacuation-list view. Consultations stay in this list (date and time, newest first); the Attention badge counts only today.

actions.label: Types
actions.text: Filter by Long shift (per team, default >10 hours), Not clocked out (per team, default >16 hours), No break (>6 hours without a live Clock Point break), Quick hop (move within 5 min) or Evacuation list (all views, with date). The No break alarm does not look at the team minimum on the timesheet.

actions.label: Action
actions.text: For an open shift, use Close shift to end it with a reason. Evacuation-list views are not a shift: they remain in this list (date and time, newest first). The nav badge counts only today’s attention.

actions.label: What do you find here?
actions.text:
On this screen you see when your workers clocked in and out, how much they worked, and at which location they signed in.

By default the screen opens on today. You can choose another period to look at earlier work.

actions.label: List or week?
actions.text:
You can view the clocked hours in two ways: List or Week.

• List: all shifts one under the other, with their registrations.
• Week: the days of one worker, with the shifts on the hours.

Weekends are hidden by default. Turn Weekends on if you also want to see Saturday and Sunday. The change applies straight away.

actions.label: Viewing the list
actions.text:
Choose the period under From and To. You can narrow the overview further by Team, Worker or Clock Point.

Click Apply to refresh the overview.

For each shift you see:

• The worker’s name and the team.
• The hours worked and the break.
• The date and, if there is one, Planned, when a shift is on the roster for that day.
• All clock-in and clock-out registrations.
• The current status of the shift.

Is All workers selected under Worker? Then you can click a name to open that worker’s week straight away, in the week of the shift.

Under a shift there can also be extra details, such as:

• Moves during this shift
• Work visits
• Tasks during this shift

actions.label: Viewing the week
actions.text:
Choose Week, select a worker under Worker and click Apply. If you have not selected anyone yet, WinProx first asks you to choose a worker.

You get an overview of every day in that week, with the shifts that belong to it.

Each block is a shift, from clock-in to clock-out. A shift that is still running continues until the current time.

The break is shown hatched. Is there also a planned shift on the roster for that day? You see it as a dotted line behind the clocked hours.

At the top you find the total hours per day and for the whole week. A full day of absence, for example leave, is shown next to the day total. Those hours do not count as worked.

Use the arrows to move to another week. Click Today to return to the current week.

Want to change something? Click a shift block. You can correct a closed shift or close a shift that is still open.

Good to know: a night shift that runs past midnight is shown on both calendar days. The hours worked count toward the day total of the day the worker clocked in.

Even when Weekends is off, a night shift that starts on Friday and continues into Saturday still counts with Friday.

actions.label: Viewing the registrations
actions.text:
Under Registrations you find every punch of a shift.

Each time you see:

• The recorded time.
• In or Out.
• The location where the worker signed in.

Breaks are also shown as a time block, for example 12:00–12:30 Break. Is the break still running? Then the block continues until the current time.

Do you use a Clock Point named Sign in? Then WinProx shows the linked site. If no site is set, it simply shows Clock Point.

actions.label: What do the statuses mean?
actions.text:
The status shows straight away what happened to a shift.

• Open: the worker is still clocked in.
• Closed: the worker clocked out normally.
• Closed (admin): an administrator closed the shift.
• Closed (automatic): WinProx closed a forgotten shift automatically. By default that happens after 16 hours. You can set this limit per team.
• Clocked in manually: an administrator clocked the worker in.

actions.label: Correcting a clocked shift
actions.text:
Did a worker forget to clock out, or is a registration wrong? Then you can adjust a closed shift.

Click Correct on the shift.

You can change:

• The clock-in time.
• The clock-out time.
• The break minutes.

You must always enter a reason. WinProx keeps who made the change and why. Every adjustment stays traceable.

If you leave the clock-out time empty, the shift opens again. That is useful, for example, when someone clocked out by mistake.

This only works if the worker does not already have another open shift.

You cannot correct an open shift directly. Close it first with Close shift.

Good to know: a correction updates the timesheet. No new clock-in or clock-out is sent to the NSSO.

actions.label: Closing an open shift
actions.text:
Did a worker forget to clock out? Then you can close the shift yourself.

On the open shift, click Close shift. WinProx closes the shift at the current time. You also give a reason.

Does the team have a minimum break, and did the shift last at least 4 hours? Then that break is included in the hours.

You can close an open shift in the same way from Presence.

actions.label: Clocking in manually
actions.text:
Does a worker not have a phone, or is it temporarily not possible to clock in? Then you can do it manually as an administrator.

Click Clock in manually and select:

• The worker.
• The Clock Point.
• The reason for the manual registration.

The worker is clocked in without a phone being linked to the registration.

The status Clocked in manually appears on the shift.

Later the worker can clock out with a QR scan. You can also close the shift as an administrator with Close shift.

actions.label: Minimum break
actions.text:
You can set a required minimum break per team.

Did a closed shift last at least 4 hours, and did the worker take less break than the minimum? Then WinProx fills the break up automatically on clock-out.

You recognise this by Filled up to … (team rule).

Was the break not filled up automatically? You can still do it with Fill up to …. You can also change the break minutes yourself with Correct.

The fill-up does not apply to shifts shorter than 4 hours, or to shifts that are still open.

Important: the filled-up break is recorded on the timesheet. It is not an extra break that was actually clocked. No new registration is sent to the NSSO either.

actions.label: Tasks during a shift
actions.text:
Does a worker use a unit QR code during the shift to start or finish a task? Then WinProx links that task to the open shift automatically.

Afterwards you can also see which tasks were done during a particular shift.

On clock-out, WinProx automatically closes any linked tasks that are still open.

actions.label: Downloading a report
actions.text:
Do you want to keep the clocked hours, process them further or print them? Click Download report.

You can choose:

• CSV: download a file you can open and edit in Excel, among other tools.
• Print (PDF): open an overview you can print or save as a pdf.

The report uses the same filters as the screen. Shifts that are not on the current page are included too.

Is Weekends off? Then Saturday and Sunday are left out of the report as well.

A report contains at most 5,000 shifts. Are there more? Shorten the period or use extra filters.

actions.label: From other screens
actions.text:
You can also open the clocked hours directly from other parts of WinProx.

• Presence: click a worker’s name. You go straight to that person’s overview, with the last three weeks as the period.
• Roster: click the tick or the dot in a day cell. WinProx shows that worker’s clocked hours on that day.

actions.label: Total and by month
actions.text: Overtime shows each worker’s balance for this calendar year up to today. The total sits next to the name, then the months. Earlier months of this year are included. On 1 January the balance starts again. The figure is time worked on closed shifts minus the published roster, minus time off already on the roster or in an open request. A full day of time off follows the week pattern or the ordinary split of the contract. Not pay.

actions.label: Team and clock point
actions.text: Filter by team or clock point and click Apply. Team shows the workers of that team. Clock point shows who has a closed shift there this year. The balance stays the year balance, including hours at another clock point.

actions.label: What is a Clock Point?
actions.text:
A Clock Point is a fixed sign-in point at a site. That can be a simple sticker with a QR code, or a clock display that keeps showing a fresh QR code.

Workers scan the QR code with their phone and then choose their name and icon. That is how they sign in to WinProx.

Important: signing in is not the same as clocking in. To clock in or out, the worker must then scan a fresh QR code again at the same place.

Tip: create a Clock Point for each site first. Then print the QR codes and put them up in the right places.

actions.label: Add a Clock Point
actions.text:
Click Add and enter the following details:
• Name: choose a clear name, for example Reception or Warehouse.
• Site: optionally link the Clock Point to the right site.
• Sort order: optionally set where the Clock Point should appear in the list.

Click Save. WinProx automatically creates a unique QR code for this Clock Point.

Tip: link each Clock Point to the right site. Later, presence and time records make it easy to see where someone clocked in.

actions.label: View and share the QR code
actions.text:
At a Clock Point, click QR to open the matching QR code.

You can then:
• View the QR code and print it directly from your browser.
• Download a Word print sheet in A6, A5 or A4. The layout matches Settings → QR print sheet.
• Copy the sign-in link or share it by email or WhatsApp.

The sign-in link is for signing in to WinProx. To actually clock in or out at a fixed punch clock, a fresh on-site QR scan is still required afterwards.

Tip: put the printed QR code somewhere easy to see, preferably near the entrance.

actions.label: QR rotation
actions.text:
At the top you find the QR rotation section.

There you set after how many months WinProx may remind you to renew the QR stickers.

Lost a sticker, or do you suspect someone is misusing the QR code? Select that Clock Point and click Renew.

After renewal, the old QR code stays valid for a few more days. Then it is refused.

Important: as long as you do not renew yourself, everything keeps working. The interval is only a reminder. WinProx does not replace the QR code automatically.

actions.label: Previous QR code
actions.text:
After a renewal you can check here whether the old QR code was still scanned in the last 7 days.

Is there a record? Then the old sticker or an earlier photo of the QR code may still be in use.

Tip: replace lost stickers or QR codes that were shared publicly as soon as possible. Then put up the new QR code.

actions.label: Clock display
actions.text:
Prefer a screen instead of a printed sticker? At a Clock Point you can link a physical clock display via Display.

The display automatically shows a rotating QR code. Workers scan it with their phone, just like a normal sticker.

More about linking the display, display hours, sound, the screensaver and Sense is in the help for the clock display itself.

actions.label: Activate or deactivate a Clock Point
actions.text:
Not using a Clock Point for a while? You can set it to Inactive.

The Clock Point is kept, but workers can no longer clock in via its QR code. WinProx also shows this clearly in the portal.

When you need the point again, simply activate it.

Tip: deactivating is usually better than deleting. That way you keep the existing data and history.

actions.label: WinProx on the phone home screen
actions.text:
On the Clock Point portal, to the right of Sign in, you find a WinProx icon.

A worker can tap it to place the sign-in page as a shortcut on the phone home screen. After that the portal opens with one tap, without an app from the App Store or Play Store.

On an iPhone that goes like this:
1. Tap ⋯ at the bottom.
2. Choose Share.
3. Tap Show more.
4. Choose Add to Home Screen.

Important: with this shortcut the worker can sign in and choose their name. To clock in or out at a fixed punch clock, a fresh QR scan of the sticker or clock display is still required.

actions.label: Push notifications on the phone
actions.text:
Workers can receive WinProx notifications on their phone. That way they stay informed of important changes even when WinProx is not open.

First, WinProx must be on the home screen as a shortcut. Use the WinProx logo with the plus for that.

Then open WinProx via that shortcut. Only there does the Enable push notifications button appear.

Tap the button and allow notifications. The button then disappears automatically.

Among other things, the worker can get a notification for:
• A changed shift.
• Approved or refused leave or time off in lieu.
• A new document or announcement.
• Still clocked in after the end of the shift.
• A new task for the worker or the team.

Good to know:
• On an iPhone, push notifications only work when WinProx is opened via the home-screen icon.
• Notifications are only received on the phone where they were set up.
• The notification itself does not contain document content.

actions.label: What is this display?
actions.text: A physical TFT screen on this clock point that shows a new QR about every 30 seconds. Workers scan the screen with their phone and land on the same sign-in portal as the sticker — a photo of the screen is only valid briefly.

actions.label: Sign in with a PIN
actions.text: No phone at hand? Tap the display, pick your first name via the letters; on an open shift choose break or clock-out, then enter your 4-digit PIN. Workers without a PIN choose one on the spot (twice). After two wrong attempts that worker is blocked for one minute. Admins reset the PIN via People → Teams → Edit.

actions.label: Pairing code
actions.text: Generate pairing code creates a one-time code (XXXX-XXXX, valid 10 minutes). Type it on the screen; the request appears here under Pairing request. Confirm only when you are sure it is your device. There is at most one display per clock point — confirming a new request replaces the old device. If a display is already linked, the bottom of this block shows which device it is, when it was paired and when it last checked in — that is also where you unlink it.

actions.label: Screen hours
actions.text: Set between which hours the screen is on, e.g. nursery 06:00–19:00. Outside this window the screen is off. Both fields empty = always on; an overnight window (e.g. 22:00–06:00) works too.

actions.label: Sound
actions.text: Use the switch to turn the sound of this display on or off. On: the display beeps on every key and after a clock-in or clock-out. Off: the display stays silent. The display picks up the choice at its next check-in (±1 minute).

actions.label: Screensaver
actions.text: During up to two configured time blocks — only on the checked weekdays — the screen shows an idle screen instead of the QR code — e.g. outside peak clock-in hours. Choose what is shown: photos (10 seconds each), an analog clock with a red second hand, a digital flip clock, a black screen (backlight off, uses the least power), or QR code — the regular QR clock then stays visible. One tap shows the QR code immediately, a second tap opens manual clock-in. Upload photos via Add photo: you crop them to a rectangle and they are resized automatically. Each clock display can use up to 12 photos: its own photos and photos for all clock displays combined. Tick Show on all clock displays for images that may appear on every screen in the organisation. The screen downloads new photos automatically at its next check-in (±1 minute) and stores them locally — deleted photos disappear from the screen as well. Offline, the last downloaded album and the clocks keep working.

actions.label: Sense
actions.text: Turn Sense on when this is a D1S. The screen then measures temperature, humidity, CO₂ and air quality. Leave it off for a D1. The same switch is on a room, via Screen. The black card belongs only to this screen. For temperature and humidity you drag or type the low, target and high marks, or you choose Winter or Summer. On 1 May this switches to summer on its own, on 1 October to winter. The target is only a guide. CO₂ asks for attention above the mark. The VOC index colours from green to red; attention follows only when a high value lasts half an hour. Sense off hides the card and stops the attention on the home screen; the marks stay saved. No issue and no task is created.

actions.label: Unlink
actions.text: Breaks the link: the display can no longer show valid QR codes and returns to pairing mode. The display_id is kept for the audit trail.

actions.label: Offline behaviour
actions.text: The display checks in every minute. After ±24 hours without server contact it shows a warning; after 7 days offline the QR stops entirely. The on-hours keep working offline.

actions.label: Documents
actions.text: Privacy policy, terms of service and other legal texts from WinProx.

actions.label: What is this screen?
actions.text: This is WinProx’s activity log: who did what, when, and in which organisation. Plain language instead of technical codes.

actions.label: Reading a row
actions.text: The bold line is the event. After it: organisation, person (or System) and time. Extra context (name, email, file, #id) appears underneath when available.

actions.label: Search
actions.text: Search by everyday words (e.g. issue, promo), organisation name, or the user’s name/email.

actions.label: Why it helps
actions.text: Useful to see who approved an issue, which promo campaign was imported, or who unsubscribed — without digging into the database.

actions.label: What is this screen?
actions.text: A physical screen at this room. It shows a QR code that changes once an hour. A scan opens the same report page as the sticker on the door. A photo of the screen works until the next hour, and not after that.

actions.label: Sense
actions.text: Turn Sense on when this is a D1S. The screen then measures temperature, humidity, CO₂ and air quality. Leave it off for a D1. The same switch is on a Clock Point. The black card belongs only to this screen. For temperature and humidity you drag or type the low, target and high marks, or you choose Winter or Summer. On 1 May this switches to summer on its own, on 1 October to winter. The target is only a guide. CO₂ asks for attention above the mark. The VOC index colours from green to red; attention follows only when a high value lasts half an hour. Sense off hides the card and stops the attention on the home screen; the marks stay saved. No issue and no task is created.

actions.label: Screen hours
actions.text: Set between which hours the screen is on, e.g. nursery 06:00–19:00. Outside this window the screen is off. Both fields empty = always on; an overnight window (e.g. 22:00–06:00) works too.

actions.label: Sound
actions.text: Use the switch to turn the sound of this screen on or off. On: the screen beeps on every key and after a press. Off: the screen stays silent. The screen picks up the choice at its next check-in (±1 minute).

actions.label: Screensaver
actions.text: During up to two configured time blocks — only on the checked weekdays — the screen shows an idle screen instead of the QR code. Choose what is shown: photos (10 seconds each), an analog clock with a red second hand, a digital flip clock, a black screen (backlight off, uses the least power), or QR code — the regular QR then stays visible. One tap shows the QR code immediately. Upload photos via Add photo: you crop them and they are resized automatically. Up to 12 photos per screen. The screen downloads new photos at its next check-in (±1 minute) and stores them locally — deleted photos disappear from the screen as well.

actions.label: QR for this room
actions.text: At the bottom you see the code the screen shows. It changes once an hour. A scan opens the same report page as the sticker on the door. The sticker itself does not change.

actions.label: Pairing code
actions.text: Generate pairing code creates a one-time code (XXXX-XXXX, valid 10 minutes). Type it on the screen; the request appears here under A screen is asking to pair. Confirm only when you are sure it is your device. There is at most one screen per room — confirming a new request replaces the old device. If a screen is already linked, this page shows which device it is and when it was paired. That is also where you unlink it.

actions.label: Unlink
actions.text: Unlink stops the device for this room. The screen can no longer show a valid QR code and returns to pairing mode. You can pair another screen afterwards.

actions.label: Offline behaviour
actions.text: The screen checks in every minute. After ±24 hours without server contact it shows a warning; after 7 days offline the QR stops entirely. The on-hours keep working offline.

actions.label: What is this screen?
actions.text: Manage gateways, sensors, alarm rules and review recent events. WinProx receives sensor events; physical sensors and protocols stay with your gateway/vendor.

actions.label: WinProx Corporate
actions.text: WinProx Corporate: alarms become approved issues with tasks; sensor readings can feed ESG. Plus API, webhooks and custom integrations.

actions.label: Edit
actions.text: You can edit or deactivate gateways, sensors and rules later. For a gateway you can also rotate the token (the old token then stops working). We do not hard-delete: events are kept.

actions.label: What is a gateway?
actions.text: A gateway is the bridge between your sensors and WinProx. Sensors often talk to a vendor gateway over LoRaWAN, Zigbee, Bluetooth or MQTT. That gateway translates the data and forwards only relevant events to WinProx (over HTTPS). WinProx does not sell sensors or gateways: here you register a logical gateway with a token so WinProx knows which organisation may receive the events.

actions.label: Create a gateway
actions.text: Create a gateway and save the token immediately — it is shown only once. Configure it in your IoT gateway (X-WinProx-Iot-Key or Bearer).

actions.label: Sensors
actions.text: Map an external sensor ID (as sent by the gateway) to a name, type and preferably a unit. For ESG measurements (Corporate), also link an active numeric ESG indicator.

actions.label: Alarm rules
actions.text: A rule decides when an event becomes an issue: operator + threshold, issue text, team and priority. While an open task exists for the same rule, new alarms are deduplicated.

actions.label: Sending events
actions.text: The gateway posts to POST /api/v1/iot/events with kind alarm or measurement. Optional: idempotency_key to avoid duplicate posts. See the API docs (IoT Connect).

actions.label: Add checklist
actions.text: Create a checklist under Work → Checklists (optionally per team or shared). Then link it per unit via Locations → edit unit. Only checklists of teams linked to the category (or shared) appear in the dropdown. Points must be ticked before OK. After saving, WinProx translates the name and items into the other languages.

actions.label: Starters
actions.text: Copy a template (cleaning, technical, security) and then adjust it.

actions.label: Enable
actions.text: Turn on Allow unit checks on the category. Units inherit this automatically. Unit check then appears on the portal for signed-in workers (both category and unit must be on). Override per unit via Advanced portal options under Locations → edit unit.

actions.label: Checklists
actions.text: Create checklists under Work → Checklists (optionally per team or shared). Optionally copy a starter (cleaning, technical, security). Then link them per unit via Locations → edit unit. Only checklists of teams linked to the category (or shared) appear in the dropdown. Points must be checked before OK. After saving, WinProx automatically translates the name and items into the other languages (Ollama); editing the source language queues translations again.

actions.label: Starters
actions.text: Under Work → Checklists you can copy a template (cleaning, technical, security) and then adjust it. Afterwards link the checklist per unit.

actions.label: OK and open tasks
actions.text: OK only stores the check (no issue). Not OK stores the check; the worker can then create a normal report. Open tasks remain separate on the portal.

actions.label: What is a unit check?
actions.text: A quick confirmation on the unit QR: OK or Not OK, with worker, timestamp and optional GPS. No separate issue on OK. Optional note (max. 500 characters) and up to 4 photos; they belong to the check, not the issue list. Unticked checklist points appear on the round task.

actions.label: Not OK
actions.text: Not OK stores the check and then lets the worker create a normal report via the portal.

actions.label: Filters
actions.text: Filter by result (OK / Not OK) and location. Open GPS to view coordinates on a map.

actions.label: Download report
actions.text: Export the filtered results (not only the current page; max. 5000 rows): CSV (table for Excel) or Print (same card layout as the backoffice list; Ctrl+P to PDF). Uses the same filters as the list.

actions.label: Webhooks
actions.text: Each check triggers unit.check.recorded so external systems (IWMS, CMMS, ERP, …) can update the round.

actions.label: Inbound API
actions.text: External systems push checks with external_unit_id (the unit's External ID). Optional external_id on the check for idempotent retries. See Unit Checks API docs.

actions.label: What do you see here?
actions.text:
Here you find an overview of all your units. A unit is a separate item at a location, such as a room, machine, vehicle or piece of equipment.

A unit can have its own QR code. People can scan it to report an issue, carry out a check or record readings.

For each unit you see:
• Name: the recognisable name of the unit.
• Location: the place where the unit is.
• Category: the type the unit belongs to.
• Active or inactive: whether the unit is currently in use.

An active unit is available for use. An inactive unit is temporarily out of use.

actions.label: Search and filter units
actions.text:
Do you have many units? You can easily narrow the list with the filters.

• Location: choose a location to see only the units at that location.
• Category: choose a category to show only units of that type.

Next to the filters you see how many units match your selection.

Want to see all units again? Choose All locations and All categories.

actions.label: Open a unit
actions.text:
Click a unit to open it.

You then go to the detail page of that location, where you can manage the selected unit.

There you can, among other things:
• View and edit the unit’s details.
• View and print the QR code.
• Add new units to the location.

Please note: you cannot change details in the general units list. There you use search and filters to find the right unit. You make changes on the location’s detail page.

actions.label: Unit checks
actions.text:
With a unit check, someone can quickly check whether a unit is in order after scanning the QR code.

For example during a cleaning round, a safety check or the inspection of a machine.

When is a unit check available?

The feature must be switched on at two levels:
• On the category, if the unit is linked to a category.
• On the unit itself.

You manage these settings under Places → Categories, or directly on the unit on the location’s detail page.

Do you also want to ask specific questions during a check? You can create a questionnaire under Work → Checklists.

actions.label: Measurements
actions.text:
With unit measurements, people can record specific values via the QR code.

For example:
• The temperature of a room.
• The mileage of a vehicle.
• A meter reading or another technical value.

How do you set this up?

For this too, the feature must be switched on for both the category and the unit.

You manage the measurement fields under Work → Unit measurements. There you decide which values people can record.

Important: unit measurements are different from unit checks. With a unit check, someone says whether something is in order. With a unit measurement, someone records a specific value.

actions.label: Overview
actions.text: Under Work → Unit measurements manage measure fields (expandable at the top) and search readings with filters. Results show time, field, value, location/unit, source and optional worker.

actions.label: Measure fields
actions.text: Expand Measure fields to view or add fields: name, type (number, yes/no, text or choice), optional unit and min/max. Only active fields can be linked to units.

actions.label: Search
actions.text: Filter by measure field and location or search by field, unit, location or value. Click GO! to search.

actions.label: Link to units
actions.text: Enable Allow unit measurements on the category and the unit. Then select which measure fields belong on that unit.

actions.label: Portal

actions.text: Corporate: POST /api/v1/units/{unit}/measurements (units:update ability). Each new reading fires webhook unit.measurement.recorded. Manage under Settings → API.
