actions.label: Overview
actions.text: Under Work → Work visits you see GPS work visits: who, where (location · unit) and start–end, one card per worker per day. The menu appears only when Time and GPS work visits are on in Settings.

actions.label: Filters
actions.text: Filter by period, worker, location or open/closed. Press Apply to refresh the list.

actions.label: Time
actions.text: Time → Presence shows the open visit of who is working now. Time → Hours shows visits per shift. CIAO remains RSZ submissions, not visit history.

actions.label: Field
actions.text: Workers start and stop work on the Clock Point portal within range of the location pin (customer) or a unit with a fixed pin. Clock-in opens paid time. When GPS on clock-in is on, a position is required.

actions.label: What do you find on this screen?
actions.text:
Here you find every worker in your organisation in one overview. That makes it easy to find someone, even when your organisation has many people.

For each worker you see:
• Name: the worker’s name.
• Team: the team the worker belongs to.
• Locations: the locations where the worker may clock in. If it says All locations, that person may clock in anywhere.
• Status: Active or Inactive.
• Colleague login: this worker is also a colleague with access to the Backoffice.
• To review: a team leader created the profile recently and it still needs to be completed.

This overview is for finding workers. You add, change or deactivate them via People → Teams.

actions.label: Search and filter
actions.text:
Use the filters at the top to find the right worker quickly:
• Search by name or email address.
• Select a team, or choose All teams.
• Select a location, or choose All locations.
• Filter on Active, Inactive or All statuses.

Next to the filters you see how many workers match your selection.

When you choose a location, workers without a specific location stay visible too. The same applies to workers whose team may clock in at every location.

actions.label: Locations
actions.text:
For each worker you see the locations where that person may clock in.

If no specific locations are set, it says All locations. The worker can then clock in at every location.

Want to change the locations? Go to People → Teams → Edit.

actions.label: Link with a colleague
actions.text:
Do you see the label Colleague login? Then this worker is linked to a colleague who also has access to the Backoffice, with their own email address and password.

Both profiles together use only one licence. You do not pay twice.

Clocking in always happens on the punch clock, with the worker’s name and icon. The Backoffice sign-in details are not used for that.

actions.label: To review
actions.text:
The button To review shows active workers that a team leader recently created via Clock Point.

For now these profiles only contain a first and last name, and they carry the label To review.

On the home screen you also find the tile New worker for this.

Open the profile via People → Teams and fill in the missing details. Save the profile, or deactivate it if the worker is not needed.

Once you have saved or deactivated the profile, it disappears from this filter.

Click To review again to return to the full overview.

actions.label: Open a worker
actions.text:
Click a worker’s name to go to the team that person belongs to.

There you can change, among other things:
• The team and the allowed locations.
• The icon that appears on the punch clock.
• The mobile number.
• The PIN and passkey.
• Whether the worker is a team leader.
• The status: Active or Inactive.

You can also delete the worker there.

You create new workers via People → Teams. You cannot do that directly from this overview.

actions.label: Documents and announcements
actions.text:
Does a worker have documents or announcements? Then you see a counter next to the name. It shows the same number as on the team page.

Move your mouse over the counter to see whether it is Manage documents or Manage announcements.

Click the counter to go straight to the team’s list. That list is then filtered to that worker.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: Shows Clock Point events sent to the NSSO (Check In and Out at Work): status, errors and NSSO id. CIAO itself is requested via info@winprox.app and enabled by a superuser.

actions.label: Filters
actions.text: Filter by status (queued, submitted, failed, skipped) or search by worker name.

actions.label: Retry
actions.text: For Failed or Skipped, queue the submission again after fixing NISS, DDT or CBE number.

actions.label: Download report
actions.text: CSV or print of the filtered CIAO submissions (same filters as this screen). No SSIN in the file.

actions.label: Retention
actions.text: Successful submissions older than the configured period (default 12 months) are deleted automatically. Failed / queued stay. The official record remains with the NSSO.

actions.label: What is the roster for?
actions.text:
With the roster you plan who works when. For each worker and each day you set the planned shifts.

Once you publish a period, workers can view their plan on Clock Point, under My roster.

actions.label: Choose a team or a location first
actions.text:
The roster loads only after you have selected a team or a location.

That keeps the overview clear, even when your organisation has many workers.

actions.label: View a week or a month
actions.text:
With Week and Month you choose how you want to view the roster.
• Click Week to go to the current week.
• Click Month to go to the current month.
• Use the arrows to move to a previous or next period.

Weekends is off by default. You then see only Monday to Friday.

In the month view there is a clear thick line between Friday and the following Monday. That keeps the weeks distinct.

Good to know: if you save the roster while Weekends is off, Saturday and Sunday stay untouched. Existing weekend shifts are not overwritten.

actions.label: Enter a shift
actions.text:
You can enter a shift in two ways:
• Type a code from the legend, for example V2.
• Type the start and end time yourself, for example 07:00-15:00.

You can also add a group straight away. For example:
• D1/G1
• 07:00-12:00/G1

A red border around a cell means the value entered is not correct. Change it before you save the roster.

Do you use the same group code at several locations? Choose the right location first. Otherwise WinProx does not know which group you mean.

An absence cannot be linked to a group.

You open the legend via Legend, next to Publish. You manage the codes under Time → Shift types. You usually set those up only once.

actions.label: Several work blocks on one day
actions.text:
One cell holds one shift by default.

Does someone work in the morning and in the evening? Then you enter both work blocks separately via Edit day.

Please note: if you type directly in a cell that already has several work blocks, you replace the whole day with one new block.

WinProx asks for confirmation before the existing blocks are replaced.

Via Edit day you can also add a note to a work block.

Days in the past are locked. Do you still want to change one? Use Correct and give a reason.

actions.label: Working with groups
actions.text:
Do you want to view the roster by group? Choose a location first.

You then see only the workers linked to that site. Floaters who may clock in at every location do not appear in this filtered roster.

You can then tick one or more groups. You can also choose Ungrouped.

The workers are then shown under a separate heading for each group.

Two things should be kept apart:
• Home group: you set this on the worker. It decides under which group heading that person appears in the roster.
• Group on the shift: you fill this in separately in the roster cell, for example G1. It is not taken over automatically from the home group.

actions.label: Colours in the roster
actions.text:
The colours help you recognise special days and situations quickly.
• Blue: a public holiday.
• Green: a replacement day.
• Grey: a fixed day off for the worker. You can still plan a shift here.
• Weekend: has its own background colour.
• Today: is marked separately.
• Locked day: also has its own colour.

Move the pointer over the date heading of a public holiday or a replacement day to see more. You also see what effect that day has on the roster.

You can select only the date cells. Worker names and the number columns cannot be selected.

Is too little staff planned on a particular day? You see that next to that day.

On a public holiday a shortfall is not shown. On a replacement day the shortfall is shown.

actions.label: Saving and publishing
actions.text: Saving and publishing are two different actions.

actions.label: Save
actions.text:
With Save you store the week or month currently on your screen, for the workers you see at that moment.

Have you made changes and do you leave the page, or move to another week or month? Then WinProx warns you that there are unsaved changes.

Save first if you want to keep your changes. Otherwise they are lost.

actions.label: Publish
actions.text:
With Publish you make the whole period visible to workers on Clock Point, under My roster.

The workers receive a notice.

Do you change something later in a period that is already published? The period stays published. The changes are announced again only when you click Publish once more.

Important: publishing has no effect on the NSSO declaration. It only makes the roster available to your workers.

actions.label: Repeat a week
actions.text:
Do you want to reuse an existing week plan for the coming weeks? Use Repeat week.

This feature is available only in the week view.

You copy the work shifts of the visible week to following weeks. You choose how many weeks to copy, up to 26 weeks.

A few rules apply when copying:
• Absences are not copied.
• Days with approved leave are skipped. WinProx reports which days are not copied because of this.
• Does a target week already contain shifts? Then WinProx skips that whole week. The other weeks are still copied.

That way existing plans are not overwritten by accident.

actions.label: Restore
actions.text:
With Restore you can put the roster back to an earlier version.

WinProx keeps restore points that include:
• The date and time of the change.
• Where the change came from.
• Which workers and days were changed.

Restore points stay available for 30 days. The list shows at most the 40 most recent restore points.

For each restore point you see in advance what will change:
• What disappears.
• What comes back.
• What is changed.

Not every earlier situation can simply be restored. That is not possible, for example, when:
• A day involved is now locked.
• A shift has since been moved to another day.
• There is approved leave on that day.

actions.label: Extra check when there are differences
actions.text:
Has the current roster changed in the meantime, or is a request still open? Then WinProx asks for confirmation first.

You see which differences there are before you restore. Your confirmation applies only to the differences shown at that moment.

Has the roster changed again in the meantime? Then WinProx does not restore. You see the new difference first.

Did the restore succeed? You can still undo that step via Undo this restore.

actions.label: Planning an absence
actions.text:
An absence code fills the whole day in the roster cell. That day does not count as hours worked.

WinProx distinguishes four kinds of absence:
• Leave
• Time off in lieu
• Sick
• Other, for example short leave or a day off of your own.

Does someone need to be absent for only part of the day, for example next to a planned work block? Open Edit day. You can then combine work and absence on the same day.

actions.label: Requests from workers
actions.text:
Workers can request leave, time off in lieu, sick leave or an Other absence themselves on Clock Point, on the Leave / Absence tile.

You handle these requests under Time → Requests.

A sick report must be approved there as well.

Sick and Other do not affect the leave balance or the time-off-in-lieu balance.

The worker can add a photo of a note. It stays with the request for 6 months. Then WinProx deletes it. Keep your own copy if you need it longer.

actions.label: Find a replacement
actions.text:
Can someone not work a planned shift? Then you can look for another worker via Replacement….

WinProx suggests workers who:
• Already have a shift that day.
• Have the setting Available for replacement.

Under Time → Shift types you can also set that workers with no planned shift may be suggested.

Do you choose a replacement? Then the following happens:
• The original work block is turned into an absence.
• The replacement gets the same time slot.
• The location and unit are taken over.

The original plan stays recognisable, and the replacement is recorded correctly.

actions.label: Compare planned and clocked
actions.text:
For a published period you can compare the planned shifts with the hours actually clocked. That includes the current day.

WinProx checks whether the worker clocked in close to the planned time.

The standard tolerance is 15 minutes:
• Up to 15 minutes early: correct.
• 15 minutes or more late: a deviation.
• More than 15 minutes early: a deviation.

A correct clock-in is shown with a green tick at the top right of the roster cell.

For a deviation or a missing clock-in you see a dot.

Click the tick or the dot to open the clocked hours of that worker on that day.

A missing punch is shown only after the planned shift has ended, or when it is a previous day.

The original clock records are always kept.

actions.label: Print the roster
actions.text:
With Print, next to the title, you open a print-friendly version of the roster.

It opens in a new window and is laid out for A4 landscape.

actions.label: The figures on the right: Statistics
actions.text:
With Statistics you open an overview on the right with the main figures per worker.

You will find, among others:
• Norm: the contractual hours, 38 hours a week by default. You set this on the worker.
• Difference: the difference between the planned hours and the contract norm.
• Planned: the total planned hours in the selected period.
• Worked: the total hours actually clocked.
• Leave: the planned leave hours.
• Lieu: the planned time-off-in-lieu hours.
• Sick: the planned sick hours.
• Other: the other planned absences.
• Flag: a warning for an incomplete work block or an open clock-in without a clock-out.

Is the contract norm not reliably available? Then WinProx leaves the figures for Norm and Difference empty.

actions.label: How is the norm calculated?
actions.text:
In the month view WinProx takes the worker’s work pattern into account.

Is no work pattern set? Then WinProx calculates the norm from the weekly norm, spread over Monday to Friday.

For public holidays WinProx uses the settings under Time → Public holidays. If no specific scheme is set, the Belgian standard applies.

Good to know: these statistics are meant as an overview and a check. WinProx does not judge here whether someone worked too much or too little. It shows the plan, the clocked hours and the related differences.

actions.label: What is a shift type?
actions.text:
A shift type is a recognisable code (for example V2 or VL) with a name and a colour. You use these codes on the roster to mark duties and absences simply.

You usually set shift types once. After that you keep using them and only change them when your organisation changes.

Tip: choose short, recognisable codes. The name may be a bit longer so everyone immediately understands what the code means.

actions.label: Add or edit
actions.text:
Click Add to create a new shift type or Edit to change an existing one.

Enter at least the code, name and kind. Then choose a colour and save.

Important: changes to an existing shift type are not applied automatically to duties already on the roster. If you change the hours, name or colour, existing duties stay as they are. Only new or re-entered duties use the updated settings.

Want to change existing duties too? Edit them manually on the roster.

actions.label: Kind: work
actions.text:
Choose Work for a normal work duty.

Enter the start time, end time and optionally the break (in minutes).

When you then type the code (for example V2) on the roster, WinProx fills in the matching hours automatically.

You can also enter free times directly, without a shift type. For example 07:00-15:00. That is handy for a one-off deviation from the usual roster.

actions.label: Kind: leave, TOIL or sick
actions.text:
Use these kinds for days when a worker is not working.

How are they recorded?
Leave, TOIL and sick have no start or end time. They apply by default to the full day and do not count as hours worked.

Requests via Clock Point
Workers can request these absences on Clock Point, on the Leave / Absence tile. You can review and approve requests under Time → Requests.

What happens to the balance?
• Leave: is deducted from the available leave balance. A half day of leave can be requested, but only when the request covers one day.
• TOIL: is linked to the overtime/TOIL arrangement. It does not affect the leave balance.
• Sick: does not affect the leave balance or TOIL. Further administrative processing of sickness happens outside WinProx.

A sick day cannot be recorded as a half day.

actions.label: Kind: other
actions.text:
Choose Other for absences that are specific to your organisation, such as short leave or a “baaldag”.

You set the code and name yourself. For example:
• KV – Short leave
• BAAL – Baaldag

These absences also have no start or end time and apply to the full day.

Requests via Clock Point
Workers can request these absences by choosing the desired name. For Other, only one day can be submitted per request.

After your approval the absence appears automatically on the roster.

Other absences do not affect the leave balance or TOIL.

actions.label: On the roster
actions.text:
Go to Time → Roster and type the desired shift-type code in a cell. WinProx fills in the matching duty or absence automatically.

Want several duties or time blocks on one day? Open Edit day.

When you approve an absence request, WinProx replaces the planned duty with the absence.

In the information tip on the cell you can still see what was originally planned. This is shown as Was planned : ….

actions.label: Available for replacement
actions.text:
On the kinds Work, Leave and TOIL you can turn on Available for replacement.

Workers who have such a shift type on their roster that day can then be suggested as possible replacements.

When you choose Replacement… on the roster, WinProx shows the available candidates.

How does that work?
When you pick a replacement, they take over the planned duty:
• The original worker is recorded as absent.
• The replacement automatically gets the same hours, location and unit.

Sick and Other can never be made available for replacement. Someone who is sick or has another absence is therefore not suggested as a possible replacement.

actions.label: Also unplanned
actions.text:
At the top of this page you find Also suggest workers with no plan. Hover the information tip for extra explanation.

This setting applies to the whole organisation and not separately per shift type.

• Unchecked: WinProx only suggests workers who already have a duty that day with Available for replacement turned on.
• Checked: WinProx also suggests active workers who have no duty that day yet. They must still be allowed to clock in at the location of the open duty.

This is handy, for example, when you have a fixed cover group that is usually not planned on the roster in advance.

actions.label: Deactivate
actions.text:
No longer using a shift type? Then you can Deactivate it.

A deactivated shift type no longer appears in new choices:
• You can no longer use the code to enter new duties on the roster.
• Workers can no longer choose the type for new absence requests.

Duties already on the roster with this code stay visible. They keep their entered hours, but are no longer linked to an active shift type. They are then treated as free time.

Want to use the shift type again later? Just Activate it.

Tip: deactivating is usually enough. You do not need to delete a shift type to stop using it.

actions.label: Scheme
actions.text: One holiday scheme for the whole company. The monthly norm in the roster applies these choices to all workers — nothing is set per person. In the roster a holiday column is tinted blue and a replacement day green.

actions.label: Effect
actions.text: The Belgian standard is already filled in: a holiday on Monday–Friday is dropped, a holiday in the weekend gets a proposed replacement day (badge Standard, to be confirmed). You only record deviations: No effect, Working day dropped or Replacement day with your own date — those rows show Recorded. Choose Standard to remove a deviation. The proposed date is a calculation proposal, not a recorded agreement — confirm it if it applies.

actions.label: Year
actions.text: Use the buttons to browse to another year, then click Save. The choices apply per holiday date.

actions.label: Rules
actions.text: Set per location how many workers per shift type must be planned at minimum every day, following the roster legend.

actions.label: Copy to another location
actions.text: Select at least one shift type and a minimum count greater than zero. Copy to… then appears if you may update another location. An empty input row does not count. Choose the target and confirm: the current input is copied, including unsaved changes. The target's existing minimum staffing is fully replaced; the source location stays unchanged.

actions.label: Indication
actions.text: The roster shows which shifts are missing (e.g. V2 missing), grouped per location and limited to visible future days. A public holiday is not counted; a replacement day is. This is an indication — it never blocks saving or publishing.

actions.label: Stale types
actions.text: Deactivated or deleted shift types stay greyed out until you remove them yourself — they never silently disappear.

actions.label: What is this screen for?
actions.text:
On this screen you handle workers’ requests for leave, time off in lieu, sick or another absence.

The worker submits the request on Clock Point, on the Leave / Absence tile. No email is sent. As soon as you approve or reject the request, the worker gets a notice on Clock Point.

Next to Requests the counter shows how many requests are still open. A card then also appears on the home screen with the number per kind, for example 1 Leave, 1 TOIL and 1 Sick.

A sick report must be approved here too. Sick and Other do not affect the leave balance or the time off in lieu balance.

actions.label: Good to know
actions.text:
• The worker chooses a type, for example Leave or Baaldag.
• The requested period cannot be in the past and lasts at most 31 days.
• For Other, the request can cover only one day.
• A half day can only be requested for leave on a single date.
• A worker cannot submit two open requests that overlap.

actions.label: The list
actions.text:
You can also filter by team, worker, Clock Point and period (from–to), as on Clocked hours. A request stays visible when it overlaps that period. A Clock Point shows requests from workers who may clock in there. With photo shows only requests that have a photo. Click Apply.

At the top you can filter the requests by All, Open, Approved, Rejected or Withdrawn.

For each request you see the worker, the type of absence, the requested days and, if there is one, a note.

After a decision you also see who approved or rejected the request.

If there is a photo, you see it with the request. WinProx keeps photos for 6 months and then deletes them. From 5 months the home screen warns you. Keep your own copy if you need them longer.

actions.label: Reviewing a request
actions.text:
On an open request, click Review.

You see the requested days and any note from the worker. If it says Half day, the request is for half a day of leave.

Are there already shifts on the roster for that period? You find them under Existing shifts.

Until you approve the request, those shifts stay in place. You can still change them on the roster in the meantime.

actions.label: Approve
actions.text:
When you approve, WinProx writes the absence into the roster straight away, for every day of the request.

The existing shifts are kept. You can still view them later in the information tip on that day, under Was planned.

A reason is not required. If you do add a note, the worker sees it on the request under Decision.

actions.label: Reject
actions.text:
When you reject, nothing changes on the roster.

You do have to enter a reason of at least 3 characters. The worker sees that reason on the request under Decision.

actions.label: The leave balance
actions.text:
For a leave request you see the balance for the year concerned:

• Yearly allowance
• Approved leave
• Planned leave
• Remaining balance
• This request

If no yearly allowance has been set, WinProx tells you.

If this request would take the remaining balance below zero, you get a warning. You can still approve the request.

For time off in lieu, sick or Other, no leave balance is shown.

actions.label: From the roster
actions.text:
You can also open an open request from the roster.

On a day with an open request there is a marker at the bottom left of the cell. The information tip says, for example, Leave requested (awaiting approval).

Click the marker. You land on this screen and that request opens straight away.

actions.label: Withdraw
actions.text:
A worker withdraws a request on Clock Point. That cannot be done from this screen.

The rules depend on the status:
• Open: a request can always be withdrawn.
• Approved: it can be withdrawn as long as the first day of the request has not yet passed. WinProx then puts the previously planned shifts back on the roster.
• Rejected: a rejected request can no longer be withdrawn.
• First day passed: once the first day of the request has passed, the worker can no longer withdraw it.

You find withdrawn requests with the Withdrawn filter.

actions.label: From favorite
actions.text: Pick a favorite round to reuse stops and title. Defaults to one-time due today; then choose the worker.

actions.label: Description
actions.text: Short one-line title for the round (e.g. «Bruges cleaning round»).

actions.label: Recurring
actions.text: On = interval, lead and first due date. Off = one-time round with only a due date (no next cycle).

actions.label: Interval
actions.text: How often the round repeats. Recurring only.

actions.label: Lead (days)
actions.text: How many days before the due date the task is created. Recurring only.

actions.label: Due date / first due date
actions.text: One-time: the planned date. Recurring: first due date of cycle 1.

actions.label: Stops — Choose
actions.text: Left: search by location, city or unit and tick. Locations with only a whole-location unit appear as one grey row (not nested under another location). Only units with unit checks. At least 2 stops.

actions.label: Stops — Route
actions.text: Right: selected stops in order (1 = first). Drag there to reorder: whole location block or units within a location. Untick removes a stop from the route.

actions.label: Select all units
actions.text: Adds all available stops to the route. You can then untick individual stops in the route.

actions.label: Team and worker
actions.text: Choose the team (required) and optionally one worker from that team.

actions.label: Task note
actions.text: Optional instruction on the task. Leave empty to use the round description.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: Your day starts here: shortcuts to a new customer or worker and today's presence. Below that, the latest customer visits.

actions.label: Tiles
actions.text: Each tile shows a count or status; clicking it opens the matching screen.

actions.label: Present now
actions.text: Workers with an open shift who are not on a break. Opens the presence board.

actions.label: Visits today
actions.text: Customer visits started today. Opens the shifts list.

actions.label: Workers
actions.text: Number of active workers. Opens the teams and workers list. If “(x without NISS)” appears, those workers lack a national register number (needed for CIAO).

actions.label: Seats in use
actions.text: Occupied seats versus your limit. Opens the subscription screen.

actions.label: Active customers
actions.text: Number of active customers. Opens the customer list.

actions.label: Clock Point QR
actions.text: Not a counter but a button: opens the Clock Point QR to show, print, share the sign-in link (including WhatsApp) or email. Pulses until the first shift has run.

actions.label: National register number missing
actions.text: A pulsing card lists active workers without a national register number. Tap a name to fill in that worker's number. Without it, CIAO cannot send their presence to the social security office. The card disappears once every number is filled in.

actions.label: Recent activity
actions.text: The eight most recent customer visits, newest first: worker, customer and work address, with start and end time — or just the start time while the visit is still running. 'Running' links to the presence list, 'Done' to the shifts list. The 'Open presence' button top right opens the live board.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: Customers are the relations you work for. Under each customer sit work addresses with a GPS pin — that pin decides where a worker can start a visit.

actions.label: Add customer
actions.text: Create a customer with a name and optionally a contact person, e-mail and phone. Then add one or more work addresses.

actions.label: Import customers
actions.text: Import customers via CSV or Excel (.xlsx). Required: name. Optional contact fields and a work address (street + postal_code + city together; optional location_name, house number, country code, DDT, GPS). The same customer name on multiple rows = multiple work addresses. Download the sample file as a template. Unknown columns or invalid rows reject the whole import.

actions.label: Recent imports
actions.text: After an import you see recent imports (30 days). Per import: file name, date, customer and work-address counts. Undo import removes customers and work addresses without visits. Addresses with visits are kept.

actions.label: Work address
actions.text: Street, number, postcode, city and the GPS pin (automatic from the address or entered manually as latitude/longitude). For work under declaration of works (30bis) also fill in the DDT reference; for private customers it may stay empty.

actions.label: Where do I find the DDT number?
actions.text: The DDT number is the official number of the Declaration of Works (NSSO/RSZ). Find it on the Social Security portal: sign in, open Aangifte van werken, go to your declarations and open the one for the customer or work site — copy the number. No access? Ask whoever filed the declaration (your customer or the main contractor). For cleaning declarations, the specific CIaO QR code or URL retrieves the number automatically.

actions.label: Edit and deactivate
actions.text: Adjust customer and work address via the row. Deactivating keeps the history: no new visit can start at an inactive address.

actions.label: Statistics
actions.text: With the Time module each customer shows the visits, worked time and visited work addresses of the current month. Click it for the statistics screen with a month picker, a per-address breakdown and export (CSV or print).

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: Workers are field staff without a login. They sign in via the Clock Point link or QR with their name and a personal icon (or PIN or biometrics), and use one fixed phone.

actions.label: Add
actions.text: Add a worker with first and last name in a team — one team is enough to start.

actions.label: NISS (CIAO)
actions.text: Fill in the NISS/INSZ number when the worker takes part in NSSO presence registration. Without NISS no submission is possible for that worker.

actions.label: Icon, phone, PIN and passkey
actions.text: Lost device, lockout or wrong icon: open Edit and release the icon, phone, PIN or passkey. The worker then signs in again.

actions.label: Team leader
actions.text: A worker with the team leader flag can release icons and devices of teammates, manage workers and take photos in the portal.

actions.label: What is a Clock Point?
actions.text: Checkmate has exactly one Clock Point (Sign in). Workers sign in there (name + icon), clock in or out, take breaks and start customer visits with GPS. The Clock Point is created automatically; you cannot add extras or deactivate it.

actions.label: QR
actions.text: Use QR to open a dialog: view/print in the browser, or download a Word print sheet (A6, A5 or A4). Use Email or WhatsApp to share the sign-in link with a worker. Once signed in, the worker opens the portal via the home-screen icon — no new scan needed. On Checkmate, clocking in and out also works from that icon, without a scan.

actions.label: QR rotation
actions.text: Under QR rotation you set an interval (months) and renew the QR (lost sticker or suspected misuse). The system recommends renewal at a random moment within that interval. The old code still works for a few days (grace period), then it is blocked.

actions.label: Previous QR code
actions.text: After renewal the previous QR still works for a few days. After that a scan is refused. A line here means that previous code was scanned again in the last 7 days.

actions.label: Edit
actions.text: You can change the Clock Point name. There is no site location or sort order — customer visits use GPS on the customer location, not this Clock Point.

actions.label: Clock Point on the phone’s home screen
actions.text: On the Clock Point portal, a WinProx icon sits to the right of Sign in. The worker taps it to put the sign-in link on the home screen. From then on the portal opens with one tap. On iPhone: ⋯ → Share → Show more → + Add to Home Screen.

actions.label: Push notifications on the phone
actions.text: The worker puts WinProx on the home screen first, using the logo with the plus. Then open that icon. The button Turn on push notifications is only inside that app. They tap it and allow notifications. The button disappears at once; the page does not need a refresh. On an iPhone this only works from the home screen icon. Only on the linked phone.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: Who is clocked in now and where: per worker the open shift and the running customer visit with customer and address. You see live who works where.

actions.label: Today's shifts
actions.text: All shifts of the day with clock-in, clock-out times and breaks.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: The hours record per worker: clocked shifts with start, end, breaks and the customer visits within the shift.

actions.label: Correct
actions.text: An administrator corrects clock-in, clock-out or break with a required reason. Leave the clock-out empty and the shift reopens — for example after a wrong clock-out.

actions.label: Download report
actions.text: Export the filtered hours as CSV, or print them as PDF via the print dialog.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: Real-time presence to the NSSO service Check In and Out at Work: IN when a customer visit starts, OUT when it ends and OUT/IN around breaks. Per submission you see status, any error and the NSSO reference.

actions.label: Statuses
actions.text: Queued (being sent), Sent, Failed and Skipped. For Failed or Skipped you can resubmit after correcting NISS, DDT or CBE number.

actions.label: Requirements
actions.text: For submissions you need your organisation's enterprise number (CBE) and the worker's NISS. The DDT reference is optional per work address.

actions.label: Retention
actions.text: Successful submissions older than twelve months are deleted automatically; the official registration stays with the NSSO.

actions.label: Company details
actions.text: Name, address and logo of your organisation — the logo appears on the portal and in mails.

actions.label: Request CIAO
actions.text: Request NSSO presence registration with your CBE (enterprise number) (or foreign VAT number). WinProx confirms activation; from then on customer visits and breaks go to the NSSO in real time. Punches from before activation are not submitted.

actions.label: Time clock
actions.text: Optional: require a PIN when workers sign in. The home-screen icon is on every Clock Point portal.

actions.label: Plan
actions.text: Checkmate charges €5 per active seat (colleague or field worker) per month. During the trial you get 25 licences to test properly — no unit or document limits. After the trial you set the seat quantity yourself; you cannot go below active seats — deactivate workers first.

actions.label: Delete data
actions.text: Administrators can delete the organisation and all data: download an export first, then finish with password and e-mail confirmation.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: The worker opens the Clock Point link from the mail once or scans the QR, picks their name and confirms with a personal icon, PIN or biometrics. That phone is linked from then on.

actions.label: Home screen
actions.text: Afterwards the WinProx icon on the home screen is enough (Android: one tap; iPhone: ⋯ → Share → Show more → scroll → + Add to Home Screen). No app store, no password.

actions.label: Other device
actions.text: A different phone is refused until an administrator or team leader releases the device — keeping one phone per worker.

actions.label: Clock in
actions.text: At the start of the workday: one tap on Clock in — via the home screen icon, no QR scan needed. Scanning the Clock Point sticker or the clock screen clocks in too. If GPS on clock-in is on, your location is required. The shift runs until you clock out.

actions.label: Break
actions.text: Start and stop breaks from the portal; they count on the hours record and — with CIAO active — go to the NSSO as OUT/IN.

actions.label: Clock out
actions.text: Clock out at the end of the day — also possible from the icon, without a scan. Clock-out closes the shift and any open customer visit. Signing out of the portal is not the same as clocking out.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: A customer visit registers work at a customer. Tap Start working at the customer — your phone checks via GPS that you are within the agreed radius. Outside the radius the visit does not start.

actions.label: Switch customer
actions.text: From customer A to customer B: the visit at A stops and the one at B starts, in one action.

actions.label: New customer on the road
actions.text: Customer not in the list? Create it on the road with name and address; the GPS pin comes from your phone. If the name looks like an existing customer you get a soft warning first.

actions.label: Navigate
actions.text: The Navigate button opens the address in your maps app — it does not register a visit.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: The worker only sees their own shifts of the selected month: per day the first clock-in, last clock-out, break and worked time. No correction and no colleagues' hours.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: How much work was done for this customer in a month? You see worked time, the number of visits and the breakdown per work address.

actions.label: Period
actions.text: Use the buttons to browse to a previous or next month. The figures follow immediately.

actions.label: What is counted?
actions.text: Worked time is the presence duration of work visits at the customer's work addresses. Shift breaks are not deducted. An ongoing visit counts up to now.

actions.label: Export or print
actions.text: Download the statistics as CSV or print them — useful as an attachment to a monthly invoice.

actions.label: What do you see on this screen?
actions.text:
Here you see what happened in your organisation. Important changes and events are kept in an activity log.

Among other things, you find:
• Adjusted or force-closed shifts, always with the reason.
• Workers who were created, changed or deleted.
• Changes to customers, locations or units.
• Changes to settings.
• Security events, such as a linked phone, a reset icon or a refused QR scan.

The newest events are at the top.

Good to know: ordinary clock-in and clock-out movements are not all recorded in this log. Follow those via Time → Hours. The activity log focuses mainly on exceptions, changes and admin actions.

actions.label: How do you read a line?
actions.text:
The bold text describes what happened — for example that a shift was corrected or that a worker was added.

After that you see who performed the action and when it happened.

If no person was involved, it may say System.

Under the event you sometimes find extra information, such as a name, email address or number.

actions.label: Filter by category
actions.text:
At the top you can filter the list by category:
• All
• Time & shifts
• Workers
• Customers & locations
• Settings
• Security & devices
• Other

Not sure where to look yet? Start with All. Then optionally choose a category to narrow the list.

actions.label: Search
actions.text:
With the search field you can search the activity log in a targeted way.

You can search for example on:
• A word from the event, such as shift or worker.
• The name or email address of the colleague who made the change.
• A number shown with the event.

Tip: use ordinary words as you see them on screen. You do not need to know technical codes.

actions.label: Who can see this?
actions.text:
Only admins of your organisation have access to this screen.

Workers, team leaders and colleagues with a normal employee role cannot view the activity log.

Good to know: this log helps you later check what changed, who did it and when. It is not a replacement for reports or timesheets.
